impact: A compromised user with a FullAccess policy grants the attacker unrestricted control over the corresponding AWS service, enabling data exfiltration, resource deletion, or privilege escalation depending on the service.
remediation_brief: Replace the full-access policy with a scoped policy granting only the permissions the user needs. Use IAM Access Analyzer to identify unused permissions.

title: RDS instance publicly accessible: {db_id}
description: RDS instance is configured as publicly accessible, meaning its endpoint resolves to a public IP.
impact: The database is reachable from the internet. An attacker can attempt authentication brute-force, exploit known database vulnerabilities, or exfiltrate data if credentials are weak or leaked.
remediation_brief: Disable public accessibility: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier <id> --no-publicly-accessible

title: RDS instance unencrypted: {db_id}
description: RDS storage encryption is not enabled.
impact: Database data at rest is unencrypted. If snapshots are shared, copied, or the underlying storage is accessed, all data (including credentials and PII) is readable in plaintext.
remediation_brief: Enable encryption at rest. For existing instances: create an encrypted snapshot, then restore from it.

title: RDS instance no automated backups: {db_id}
description: Automated backups are disabled on the RDS instance (retention period is 0 days).
impact: Without automated backups, data loss from accidental deletion, corruption, or ransomware is permanent. Point-in-time recovery is unavailable.
remediation_brief: Enable automated backups with an appropriate retention period (minimum 7 days recommended).

title: RDS instance deletion protection disabled: {db_id}
description: Deletion protection is disabled on the RDS instance — the database can be deleted without safeguard.
impact: An attacker or careless operator with sufficient IAM permissions can delete the production database with a single API call, causing total data loss and service outage.
remediation_brief: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier <id> --deletion-protection

title: RDS instance not Multi-AZ: {db_id}
description: Multi-AZ deployment is not enabled — there is no standby replica for automatic failover.
impact: A single availability zone failure causes a full database outage with no automatic failover. Recovery time depends on snapshot restore, which can take hours for large databases.
remediation_brief: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier <id> --multi-az

title: CloudTrail: No CloudTrail trails configured
description: No CloudTrail trails exist in this region/account. API activity is not logged.
impact: Without CloudTrail, all AWS API calls go unrecorded. Attackers can operate undetected — creating users, exfiltrating data, modifying resources — with no audit trail for incident response.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: Create a multi-region CloudTrail trail logging to a dedicated, encrypted S3 bucket.

title: CloudTrail not actively logging: {trail_name}
description: CloudTrail trail exists but is not actively logging.
impact: The trail is configured but disabled, so API calls are not being recorded. An attacker may have stopped logging to cover their tracks, or operational drift disabled it. All activity during the gap is invisible.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: aws cloudtrail start-logging --name <trail>

title: CloudTrail not encrypted with KMS: {trail_name}
description: CloudTrail trail log files are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key.
impact: Without KMS encryption, log file integrity depends solely on S3 bucket security. A customer-managed KMS key provides an additional layer of access control and audit via KMS key policies.
remediation_brief: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <trail> --kms-key-id <key-arn>

title: CloudTrail not integrated with CloudWatch Logs: {trail_name}
description: CloudTrail trail does not deliver events to CloudWatch Logs for real-time alerting.
impact: Without CloudWatch Logs integration, security events (root login, unauthorized API calls, resource deletions) cannot trigger real-time alarms. Detection and response are delayed until manual log review.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: Configure a CloudWatch Logs log group and IAM role for the trail to enable real-time event delivery.

title: KMS key rotation disabled: {key_id}
description: Automatic key rotation is not enabled for this customer-managed KMS key.
impact: Without rotation, the same key material protects data indefinitely. If the key is ever compromised, all data encrypted since key creation is at risk rather than just the current rotation period.
remediation_brief: aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id <key-id>

title: Lambda function environment contains secrets: {fn_name}
description: Lambda function has environment variables with secret-like names (passwords, API keys, tokens). These are visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunction or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration permission.
impact: Secrets in Lambda environment variables are stored in plaintext and accessible via the AWS API. Any principal with read access to the function configuration can extract credentials and pivot to the systems they protect.
remediation_brief: Move secrets to AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them at runtime.

title: Lambda function publicly invokable: {fn_name}
description: Lambda function has a resource-based policy granting Principal=* with no Condition — anyone can invoke this function.
impact: Any AWS account or anonymous caller can invoke the function, potentially triggering unintended actions, exhausting concurrency limits, incurring costs, or exploiting vulnerabilities in the function code.
remediation_brief: Restrict the resource policy Principal to specific AWS accounts or services, or add a Condition key (e.g., aws:SourceArn).

title: Lambda function URL without authentication: {fn_name}
description: Lambda function has a function URL with AuthType=NONE — anyone on the internet can invoke it without credentials.
impact: The function URL is a public HTTPS endpoint with no authentication. Attackers can invoke the function directly, abuse its functionality, cause cost spikes, or exploit vulnerabilities in the handler code.
remediation_brief: Set AuthType to AWS_IAM on the function URL, or add a CloudFront distribution with WAF in front.

title: Lambda function uses deprecated runtime: {fn_name} ({runtime})
description: Lambda function runs on a deprecated runtime that no longer receives security patches.
impact: Deprecated runtimes accumulate unpatched vulnerabilities. An attacker exploiting a known runtime vulnerability can achieve code execution within the Lambda execution environment and access the function's IAM role credentials.
remediation_brief: Upgrade the function runtime to the latest supported version for the language.

title: VPC without flow logs: {vpc_id}
description: VPC does not have VPC Flow Logs enabled — network traffic is not auditable.
impact: Without flow logs, network-level anomalies (lateral movement, data exfiltration, port scanning) cannot be detected or investigated. Incident response lacks network forensic evidence.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids <vpc-id> --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs

title: Default security group has inbound rules: {sg_id}
description: The default security group has non-empty inbound rules. Resources assigned to the default SG inherit these rules.
impact: Resources accidentally placed in the default security group inherit permissive inbound rules. This is a common misconfiguration that silently exposes new resources to unintended network access.
remediation_brief: Remove all inbound and outbound rules from the default security group in every VPC.
category: Default security group has inbound rules

title: EFS file system publicly accessible: {fs_name}
description: EFS file system has a resource policy granting Principal=* — any AWS principal can mount and access the filesystem.
impact: Any AWS account can mount the EFS share and read or write all files. Sensitive data, configuration files, and application code on the filesystem are fully exposed.
remediation_brief: Restrict the EFS resource policy to specific AWS accounts, VPCs, or IAM roles.

title: SNS topic not encrypted with KMS: {topic_name}
description: SNS topic does not use a KMS key for server-side encryption.
impact: Messages published to the topic are stored unencrypted. If the SNS service is compromised or messages are intercepted, sensitive notification payloads (alerts, PII, tokens) are readable in plaintext.
remediation_brief: aws sns set-topic-attributes --topic-arn <arn> --attribute-name KmsMasterKeyId --attribute-value <key-id>
category: SNS topic not encrypted with KMS

title: SNS topic publicly accessible: {topic_name}
description: SNS topic has a resource policy granting Principal=* without a Condition restricting access.
impact: Any AWS account or service can publish to or subscribe to the topic. Attackers can inject malicious messages, subscribe to exfiltrate notification data, or abuse the topic for spam/phishing delivery.
remediation_brief: Restrict the SNS topic policy Principal to specific AWS accounts, services, or add a Condition key.

title: SQS queue not encrypted: {queue_name}
description: SQS queue has neither KMS-managed nor SQS-managed server-side encryption enabled.
impact: Messages in the queue are stored unencrypted. If an attacker gains queue read access, message payloads (which may contain PII, tokens, or commands) are readable in plaintext.
remediation_brief: aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url <url> --attributes SqsManagedSseEnabled=true

title: SQS queue publicly accessible: {queue_name}
description: SQS queue has a resource policy granting Principal=* without a Condition restricting access.
impact: Any AWS account can send, receive, and delete messages from the queue. Attackers can inject poisoned messages, steal queued data, or disrupt processing by purging the queue.
remediation_brief: Restrict the SQS queue policy Principal to specific AWS accounts or services.

title: GuardDuty: Not enabled
description: Amazon GuardDuty is not enabled in this region — threat detection for the account is absent.
impact: Without GuardDuty, automated threat detection (compromised credentials, cryptocurrency mining, data exfiltration patterns, unusual API behavior) is not active. Attacks proceed undetected.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: aws guardduty create-detector --enable

title: Security Hub: Not enabled
description: AWS Security Hub is not enabled in this region — centralized security posture management is absent.
impact: Without Security Hub, there is no unified view of security findings across AWS services. Compliance checks (CIS Benchmarks, PCI DSS, AWS Foundational Best Practices) do not run, and cross-service correlation is unavailable.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: aws securityhub enable-security-hub

title: ACM certificate expired or expiring soon: {domain}
description: ACM certificate has expired or will expire within 30 days.
impact: Expired certificates cause TLS handshake failures, breaking HTTPS connectivity for end users. Services behind the certificate become unavailable or fall back to insecure connections.
remediation_brief: Renew or replace the ACM certificate. Verify DNS or email validation is configured for auto-renewal.
category: ACM certificate expired or expiring soon

title: CloudWatch log groups without KMS encryption ({count} group(s))
description: CloudWatch log groups are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key.
impact: Log data (which may contain sensitive application output, error messages with PII, or security events) is not protected by customer-managed encryption. Access control relies solely on IAM policies.
remediation_brief: aws logs associate-kms-key --log-group-name <name> --kms-key-id <key-arn>

title: CloudWatch log groups without retention policy ({count} group(s))
description: CloudWatch log groups have no retention policy set (logs retained indefinitely).
impact: Indefinite retention incurs growing storage costs and increases the blast radius of a log data breach. Conversely, if retention is too short, forensic evidence may be lost before an incident is detected.
remediation_brief: aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name <name> --retention-in-days <days>

title: ECS task definition contains secrets in environment: {task_def}/{container}
description: ECS task definition has environment variables with secret-like names (passwords, API keys, tokens) in plaintext.
impact: Plaintext secrets in task definitions are visible via the ECS API to any principal with ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition. Container environment variables are also exposed via the task metadata endpoint inside the container.
remediation_brief: Use ECS secrets (valueFrom) referencing Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store instead of plaintext environment variables.
category: ECS task definition contains secrets in environment

title: OpenSearch domain publicly accessible: {domain_name}
description: OpenSearch domain is not deployed inside a VPC — the endpoint is accessible from the public internet.
impact: The OpenSearch endpoint is directly reachable from the internet. If access policies are misconfigured, any attacker can query, modify, or delete indices containing sensitive data.
remediation_brief: Migrate the OpenSearch domain into a VPC. Note: this requires domain recreation for existing public domains.

title: OpenSearch domain encryption at rest disabled: {domain_name}
description: OpenSearch domain does not have encryption at rest enabled.
impact: Index data on the underlying storage is unencrypted. If storage is compromised or snapshots are exfiltrated, all indexed data (which may contain PII, logs, or sensitive application data) is readable in plaintext.
remediation_brief: Enable encryption at rest in the OpenSearch domain configuration.
category: OpenSearch domain encryption at rest disabled

title: Secrets Manager secret rotation disabled: {secret_name}
description: Secrets Manager secret does not have automatic rotation enabled.
impact: Without automatic rotation, secrets remain static indefinitely. If a secret is compromised, it remains valid until manually rotated, giving attackers a persistent access window.
remediation_brief: Configure automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function.

title: CloudFront distribution access logging disabled: {distribution}
description: CloudFront distribution does not have access logging enabled.
impact: Without access logs, malicious requests, bot traffic, and data exfiltration via the CDN cannot be detected or investigated after the fact.
owasp_web: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: Enable standard or real-time access logging to an S3 bucket.

title: CloudFront distribution without WAF: {distribution}
description: CloudFront distribution does not have an AWS WAF WebACL attached.
impact: Without WAF, the distribution has no application-layer filtering. SQL injection, XSS, bot traffic, and volumetric attacks reach the origin server unfiltered.
remediation_brief: Associate an AWS WAF WebACL with the CloudFront distribution.

title: CloudFront distribution allows HTTP: {distribution}
description: CloudFront distribution default cache behavior allows HTTP (ViewerProtocolPolicy=allow-all).
impact: Viewers can connect over plaintext HTTP, exposing request and response data to network eavesdroppers. Session tokens, API keys, and user data transmitted over HTTP can be intercepted.
remediation_brief: Set ViewerProtocolPolicy to redirect-to-https or https-only in the default cache behavior.

title: DynamoDB table not using customer-managed encryption: {table_name}
description: DynamoDB table is using default AWS-owned encryption or has no explicit SSE configuration. Customer-managed KMS keys provide better audit control.
impact: With AWS-owned keys, the customer has no visibility into key usage via CloudTrail and cannot enforce key policies or rotation schedules. Regulatory frameworks may require customer-managed key controls.
remediation_brief: aws dynamodb update-table --table-name <table> --sse-specification Enabled=true,SSEType=KMS,KMSMasterKeyId=<key-arn>
category: DynamoDB table not using customer-managed encryption

title: Scope Limitations: Insufficient permissions for {n} AWS service(s)
description: The audit credentials lack permissions for one or more AWS services. Findings for these services may be incomplete.
impact: Incomplete audit coverage — security misconfigurations in denied services go undetected, potentially leaving vulnerabilities unaddressed.
remediation_brief: Grant the audit IAM user/role read-only access to the denied services to enable comprehensive coverage.

title: Vertex AI: Model endpoint not using VPC peering: {endpoint}
aliases: Vertex AI Model Not Using VPC Peering
description: Vertex AI model endpoint is not configured with VPC peering for private connectivity. Inference traffic traverses public Google APIs instead of remaining within a private network boundary.
impact: An attacker with network visibility can intercept or observe model inference requests and responses transiting public APIs. Sensitive prompts, model inputs, and prediction outputs may be exposed.
remediation_brief: Configure VPC peering or Private Service Connect on the Vertex AI endpoint to keep model traffic within a private network.

title: Vertex AI: Endpoint public access enabled: {endpoint}
aliases: Vertex AI Endpoint Public Access Enabled
description: Vertex AI endpoint allows public internet access without VPC peering or Private Service Connect. Model inference requests are reachable from any network.
impact: An attacker can send inference requests to the publicly accessible endpoint, potentially abusing the model for prompt injection, data exfiltration through crafted inputs, or running up compute costs via denial-of-wallet attacks.
remediation_brief: Restrict the Vertex AI endpoint to private access via VPC peering or Private Service Connect. Deny public internet connectivity.

title: Vertex AI: Model monitoring not configured
aliases: Vertex AI Model Monitoring Not Configured
description: No Vertex AI model monitoring jobs exist. Without monitoring, data drift, prediction drift, and feature attribution skew go undetected.
impact: Model quality degrades silently over time. An attacker who poisons training data or manipulates inputs can cause biased or incorrect predictions without triggering any alert. Compliance frameworks requiring model governance are unsatisfied.
remediation_brief: Create a Vertex AI Model Monitoring job to detect drift, skew, and anomalies in model predictions.

title: Vertex AI: Pipeline logging disabled
description: Cloud Audit Logs are not explicitly configured for Vertex AI (aiplatform.googleapis.com). Pipeline executions, model deployments, and prediction requests may not be auditable.
impact: Without audit logs, unauthorized model access, data exfiltration through predictions, or pipeline tampering leave no forensic trail. Incident response and compliance evidence gathering are impaired.
remediation_brief: Enable Cloud Audit Logs for aiplatform.googleapis.com with DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE log types.

title: Vertex AI: Workbench notebook has public IP: {notebook}
aliases: Vertex AI Workbench Notebook Public IP
description: Vertex AI Workbench managed notebook has an external IP address. Notebooks contain code, credentials, and data; public exposure increases the attack surface.
impact: An attacker can target the notebook directly from the internet. Exposed Jupyter endpoints may allow unauthenticated code execution, credential theft, or lateral movement into the GCP project.
remediation_brief: Recreate the notebook with --no-public-ip or configure Private Google Access on the subnet.

title: Vertex AI: Feature Store no CMEK: {featurestore}
aliases: Vertex AI Feature Store No Encryption
description: Vertex AI Feature Store does not use a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK). Data is encrypted with Google-managed keys only, reducing control over key rotation and access.
impact: The organization cannot enforce its own key rotation schedule, revoke keys independently of Google, or meet regulatory requirements mandating customer-controlled encryption. A compromised Google-managed key exposes feature data.
remediation_brief: Recreate the Feature Store with --encryption-spec-kms-key-name pointing to a Cloud KMS key you manage.

title: Azure OpenAI: Public network access enabled: {account}
aliases: Azure OpenAI Public Network Access Enabled
description: Azure OpenAI service has public network access enabled with no network ACL restriction. Model endpoints are reachable from the public internet.
impact: An attacker can send requests to the public API endpoint using stolen or leaked API keys. This enables prompt injection attacks, model abuse, data exfiltration through crafted prompts, and denial-of-wallet via compute exhaustion.
remediation_brief: Disable public network access or set network ACL default action to Deny with explicit IP/VNet allow rules.

title: Azure OpenAI: Content filtering not configured: {account}
aliases: Azure OpenAI Content Filtering Not Configured
description: Azure OpenAI deployment(s) do not have a content filtering (RAI) policy attached. Prompts and completions are not screened for harmful content.
impact: Without content filtering, the model can generate or accept harmful, biased, or inappropriate content. This exposes the organization to reputational risk, regulatory non-compliance, and potential legal liability.
remediation_brief: Assign a content filter policy to each Azure OpenAI deployment via Azure AI Studio or the REST API.

title: Azure OpenAI: Diagnostic logging disabled: {account}
description: Azure OpenAI account has no diagnostic settings configured. API calls, content filtering events, and operational metrics are not being logged for audit or incident response.
impact: Without diagnostic logging, unauthorized API usage, prompt injection attempts, and content filter bypasses leave no audit trail. Incident response is blind and compliance with logging requirements (PCI DSS 10, SOC 2 CC7) is unmet.
remediation_brief: Create a diagnostic setting to send Azure OpenAI logs to Log Analytics workspace, Storage Account, or Event Hub.

title: Azure OpenAI: Managed identity not used: {account}
aliases: Azure OpenAI Managed Identity Not Used
description: Azure OpenAI account does not use a managed identity (system-assigned or user-assigned). Authentication relies on API keys, which can be leaked, shared, or difficult to rotate.
impact: API key-based auth cannot be scoped per caller, audited at identity granularity, or automatically rotated. Leaked keys grant full access to all model deployments until manually regenerated.
remediation_brief: Enable a system-assigned or user-assigned managed identity and use Azure RBAC for authentication instead of API keys.

title: Azure OpenAI: Customer-managed key not configured: {account}
aliases: Azure OpenAI Customer-Managed Key Not Configured
description: Azure OpenAI account does not use a customer-managed key (CMK) for encryption at rest. Data is encrypted with Microsoft-managed keys, reducing customer control over key lifecycle and access policies.
impact: The organization cannot enforce its own key rotation, revocation, or access logging policies. Regulatory requirements mandating customer-controlled encryption (PCI DSS 3.5, NIST SC-12) may be unmet.
remediation_brief: Configure a customer-managed key from Azure Key Vault for the Cognitive Services account encryption.

title: Web Misconfiguration: Internal Redirect: Trailing Slash Mismatch
remediation_brief: Ensure consistent URL handling and redirect policies are configured on the web server.
description: The server issued an internal redirect due to a trailing slash mismatch on the target URL. This may expose URL normalization behavior.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Ensure consistent URL handling and redirect policies are configured on the web server.

title: Web Misconfiguration: HTTP Redirect to In-Scope URL
remediation_brief: Review redirect configurations to ensure they are intentional and do not expose sensitive routing information.
description: The target URL issues an HTTP redirect to another in-scope URL. Redirect chains may expose internal routing logic.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Review redirect configurations to ensure they are intentional and do not expose sensitive routing information.

title: Web Misconfiguration: HTTP Redirect to External URL
remediation_brief: Validate and whitelist all redirect destinations. Avoid unvalidated redirects to external URLs.
description: The target URL issues an HTTP redirect to an external domain. This could be leveraged in open redirect or phishing scenarios.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Validate and whitelist all redirect destinations. Avoid unvalidated redirects to external URLs.

title: Information Disclosure: WordPress readme.html Accessible
remediation_brief: Remove or restrict access to readme.html via web server configuration.
description: The WordPress readme.html file is publicly accessible. This file may disclose the WordPress version and other installation details.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Remove or restrict access to readme.html via web server configuration.

title: Information Disclosure: WordPress license.txt Accessible
remediation_brief: Remove or restrict access to license.txt via web server configuration.
description: The WordPress license.txt file is publicly accessible. While not directly exploitable, it confirms a WordPress installation.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Remove or restrict access to license.txt via web server configuration.

title: Information Disclosure: WordPress Version
remediation_brief: Remove version disclosure from meta generator tags and restrict access to files that reveal version information. Keep WordPress updated.
description: The WordPress version was identified from publicly accessible files or meta tags. A known version allows attackers to target specific vulnerabilities.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Remove version disclosure from meta generator tags and restrict access to files that reveal version information. Keep WordPress updated.

title: Web Misconfiguration: WordPress Login Page Accessible
remediation_brief: Restrict access to wp-login.php by IP, add CAPTCHA, implement account lockout, or use a WAF rule to limit login attempts.
description: The WordPress admin login page (wp-login.php) is publicly accessible. This exposes the authentication endpoint to brute-force and credential stuffing attacks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak or missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access protected resources.
_x_remediation: Restrict access to wp-login.php by IP, add CAPTCHA, implement account lockout, or use a WAF rule to limit login attempts.

title: Web Misconfiguration: WordPress User Registration Enabled
remediation_brief: Disable user registration if not required. If required, implement email verification and role restrictions for new registrations.
description: WordPress user self-registration is enabled. Attackers may create accounts to gain authenticated access or exploit subscriber-level vulnerabilities.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Disable user registration if not required. If required, implement email verification and role restrictions for new registrations.

title: Web Misconfiguration: WordPress Password Reset Form Accessible
remediation_brief: Implement rate limiting on the password reset endpoint and ensure username/email enumeration is not possible through error messages.
description: The WordPress password reset form is accessible. Combined with user enumeration, this could facilitate account takeover via password reset abuse.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Implement rate limiting on the password reset endpoint and ensure username/email enumeration is not possible through error messages.

title: Misconfigured Security Header: WordPress X-Pingback Header Present
remediation_brief: Disable XML-RPC or remove the X-Pingback header via web server configuration if XML-RPC functionality is not required.
description: The X-Pingback HTTP header is present, advertising the XML-RPC pingback endpoint. This confirms XML-RPC is enabled and may facilitate SSRF or DDoS amplification.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Input validation failures may allow injection attacks, data manipulation, or unauthorized code execution.
_x_remediation: Disable XML-RPC or remove the X-Pingback header via web server configuration if XML-RPC functionality is not required.

title: RPC: WordPress XML-RPC Interface Enabled
remediation_brief: Disable XML-RPC entirely if not required. If required, restrict access by IP and disable the multicall method.
description: The WordPress XML-RPC interface (xmlrpc.php) is enabled and accessible. This legacy interface enables brute-force attacks, SSRF via pingback, and DDoS amplification.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak or missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access protected resources.
_x_remediation: Disable XML-RPC entirely if not required. If required, restrict access by IP and disable the multicall method.

title: RPC: WordPress XML-RPC Multicall Brute-Force Vector
remediation_brief: Disable XML-RPC or specifically block the system.multicall method. Implement per-IP rate limiting at the web server level.
description: The XML-RPC system.multicall method is enabled, allowing an attacker to test hundreds of username/password combinations in a single HTTP request, bypassing standard rate limiting.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak or missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access protected resources.
_x_remediation: Disable XML-RPC or specifically block the system.multicall method. Implement per-IP rate limiting at the web server level.

title: RPC: WordPress XML-RPC Pingback SSRF Vector
remediation_brief: Disable XML-RPC or block the pingback.ping method. Implement egress filtering to restrict outbound requests from the web server.
description: The XML-RPC pingback.ping method is accessible. An attacker can abuse this to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or use the WordPress server as a DDoS reflector.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Input validation failures may allow injection attacks, data manipulation, or unauthorized code execution.
_x_remediation: Disable XML-RPC or block the pingback.ping method. Implement egress filtering to restrict outbound requests from the web server.

title: RPC: WordPress XML-RPC Interface Accessible
remediation_brief: Disable xmlrpc.php entirely unless required. If required, restrict access by IP whitelist.
description: The WordPress XML-RPC endpoint responds to requests. The full list of available methods was retrieved, confirming the attack surface exposed by this legacy interface.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Disable xmlrpc.php entirely unless required. If required, restrict access by IP whitelist.

title: Web Misconfiguration: WordPress REST API Exposed
remediation_brief: Restrict REST API access to authenticated users where possible. Disable specific endpoints that expose sensitive data.
description: The WordPress REST API is publicly accessible without authentication. This may expose site structure, user data, and plugin information to unauthenticated users.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Restrict REST API access to authenticated users where possible. Disable specific endpoints that expose sensitive data.

title: Enumeration: WordPress Users Exposed via REST API
remediation_brief: Disable or restrict the /wp/v2/users endpoint. Use a security plugin or custom code to require authentication for user enumeration endpoints.
description: The WordPress REST API /wp/v2/users endpoint returns a list of registered usernames and IDs without authentication. This facilitates targeted brute-force and social engineering attacks.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Disable or restrict the /wp/v2/users endpoint. Use a security plugin or custom code to require authentication for user enumeration endpoints.

title: Enumeration: WordPress Media Files Enumerable via REST API
remediation_brief: Restrict the media REST API endpoint to authenticated users or disable it if not needed for public consumers.
description: The WordPress REST API /wp/v2/media endpoint exposes a list of uploaded media files without authentication, revealing site content structure and potentially sensitive file paths.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Restrict the media REST API endpoint to authenticated users or disable it if not needed for public consumers.

title: Enumeration: WordPress User Enumeration via Author Archives
remediation_brief: Disable author archive pages or suppress the username slug from archive URLs using a security plugin or custom rewrite rules.
description: WordPress author archive pages (/?author=N) redirect to /author/<username>/, disclosing valid usernames. Enumerated usernames can be used for targeted brute-force attacks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Disable author archive pages or suppress the username slug from archive URLs using a security plugin or custom rewrite rules.

title: Enumeration: WordPress Username Disclosed via oEmbed API
remediation_brief: Disable the oEmbed endpoint if not required, or customize the author name field to avoid exposing login usernames.
description: The WordPress oEmbed endpoint discloses the site author username in its JSON response. This provides an additional username enumeration vector.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Disable the oEmbed endpoint if not required, or customize the author name field to avoid exposing login usernames.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: WordPress Configuration Backup Exposed
remediation_brief: Immediately remove all backup and temporary copies of wp-config.php from the web root. Rotate all credentials disclosed. Configure the web server to deny access to .bak, .swp, and ~ files.
description: A WordPress configuration backup file (e.g., wp-config.php.bak, wp-config.php~) was found accessible on the web server. These files typically contain database credentials, authentication keys, and salts.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Immediately remove all backup and temporary copies of wp-config.php from the web root. Rotate all credentials disclosed. Configure the web server to deny access to .bak, .swp, and ~ files.

title: Software Identified: WordPress Plugin Detected
aliases: WordPress Plugins Detected in Page Source
remediation_brief: Keep all WordPress plugins updated to the latest release. Remove readme.txt from plugin directories on production servers. Remove unused plugins to reduce attack surface.

validation_tools.name: WPScan
validation_tools.install: gem install wpscan  OR  docker pull wpscanteam/wpscan

nuclei -u TARGET -t cves/ -t vulnerabilities/ -t exposures/
nuclei -u TARGET -tags sqli,xss,ssrf

description: WordPress plugin(s) confirmed via readme.txt enumeration. Version disclosure enables targeted CVE lookups. Plugin names and versions are listed in the Affected field.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Unpatched software contains known vulnerabilities with potentially available exploit code.
_x_remediation: Keep all WordPress plugins updated to the latest release. Remove readme.txt from plugin directories on production servers. Remove unused plugins to reduce attack surface.

title: Software Identified: WordPress Theme Detected
remediation_brief: Keep themes updated. Remove inactive themes. Restrict access to theme readme and style.css version disclosures.
description: The active WordPress theme was detected via static asset paths. Theme identification aids in locating theme-specific vulnerabilities.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening.
_x_remediation: Keep themes updated. Remove inactive themes. Restrict access to theme readme and style.css version disclosures.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: WordPress Debug Log Accessible
remediation_brief: Disable WP_DEBUG in production. Move the debug log outside the web root or restrict access via web server configuration.
description: The WordPress debug log file (wp-content/debug.log) is publicly accessible. Debug logs may contain PHP errors, stack traces, file paths, database queries, and credentials.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Disable WP_DEBUG in production. Move the debug log outside the web root or restrict access via web server configuration.

title: Information Disclosure: WordPress uploads Directory Browsing Enabled
remediation_brief: Disable directory listing in the web server configuration. Add an Options -Indexes directive or equivalent.
description: Directory listing is enabled on the WordPress uploads directory. Attackers can enumerate all uploaded files, potentially finding sensitive documents or user data.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Disable directory listing in the web server configuration. Add an Options -Indexes directive or equivalent.

title: Information Disclosure: Robots.txt Discloses Hidden Paths
remediation_brief: Review paths listed in robots.txt. Ensure sensitive paths are protected by authentication, not just excluded from crawlers.
description: The robots.txt file contains Disallow directives that reveal hidden or sensitive application paths. These paths are often administrative interfaces, backup files, or unlinked endpoints.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Review paths listed in robots.txt. Ensure sensitive paths are protected by authentication, not just excluded from crawlers.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Sitemap.xml Discovered
remediation_brief: Review all URLs listed in sitemap.xml to ensure none expose sensitive functionality without proper access controls.
description: A sitemap.xml file was found. Sitemaps enumerate application URLs and can reveal non-linked endpoints and application structure.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Review all URLs listed in sitemap.xml to ensure none expose sensitive functionality without proper access controls.

title: Information Disclosure: Server Banner Disclosure
remediation_brief: Configure the web server to suppress or genericize the Server header. Remove version information from all HTTP response headers.
description: The HTTP Server header discloses the web server software name and version. This information assists attackers in identifying applicable CVEs and exploit modules.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Configure the web server to suppress or genericize the Server header. Remove version information from all HTTP response headers.

title: Information Disclosure: X-Powered-By Header Discloses Technology Stack
remediation_brief: Remove or suppress the X-Powered-By header in web server and application framework configuration.
description: The X-Powered-By HTTP response header discloses the backend technology (e.g., PHP version, ASP.NET version, Express). This aids fingerprinting and CVE targeting.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Remove or suppress the X-Powered-By header in web server and application framework configuration.

title: Information Disclosure: Application Error Message Disclosure
remediation_brief: Configure custom error pages for all HTTP error codes. Ensure verbose errors are logged server-side only and not returned to clients.
description: Verbose error messages are returned by the application, potentially revealing stack traces, file paths, database queries, or framework internals.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Configure custom error pages for all HTTP error codes. Ensure verbose errors are logged server-side only and not returned to clients.

title: Information Disclosure: Directory Listing Enabled
remediation_brief: Disable directory listing in web server configuration (Options -Indexes for Apache, autoindex off for Nginx).
description: Directory listing is enabled on one or more paths, allowing unauthenticated users to browse file and directory contents. This may expose source code, configuration files, or sensitive documents.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Disable directory listing in web server configuration (Options -Indexes for Apache, autoindex off for Nginx).

title: Sensitive File Exposed: WSDL/WADL Service Description Exposed
remediation_brief: Restrict access to WSDL/WADL files by IP or authentication. Remove them from public-facing endpoints in production.
description: A WSDL or WADL service description file is publicly accessible. These files describe all available service methods, parameters, and data types, providing a full attack surface map.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Restrict access to WSDL/WADL files by IP or authentication. Remove them from public-facing endpoints in production.

title: Discovery: GraphQL Endpoint Detected
remediation_brief: Disable introspection in production. Implement query depth limiting, rate limiting, and field-level authorization checks.
description: A GraphQL endpoint was detected. GraphQL endpoints expose a queryable schema and may be subject to introspection, batching attacks, and authorization bypass.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Input validation failures may allow injection attacks, data manipulation, or unauthorized code execution.
_x_remediation: Disable introspection in production. Implement query depth limiting, rate limiting, and field-level authorization checks.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Swagger/OpenAPI Documentation Exposed
remediation_brief: Restrict access to API documentation in production. If public documentation is required, ensure it does not expose internal or administrative endpoints.
description: Swagger UI or OpenAPI specification files are publicly accessible without authentication. These documents expose the full API surface including endpoints, parameters, authentication schemes, and data models.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Restrict access to API documentation in production. If public documentation is required, ensure it does not expose internal or administrative endpoints.

title: Admin Endpoint Exposed
remediation_brief: Restrict admin interface access by IP whitelist. Move admin interfaces to non-standard ports or behind a VPN. Enforce MFA on all administrative accounts.
description: An administrative interface was discovered at a predictable path. Admin interfaces exposed to the internet are high-value targets for brute-force, credential stuffing, and authentication bypass attacks.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak or missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access protected resources.
_x_remediation: Restrict admin interface access by IP whitelist. Move admin interfaces to non-standard ports or behind a VPN. Enforce MFA on all administrative accounts.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Backup File Discovered
remediation_brief: Remove all backup files from the web root. Add web server rules to deny access to common backup file extensions.
description: A backup file (e.g., .bak, .old, .orig, ~, .zip) was discovered in the web root. Backup files often contain source code, configuration, or credentials.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Remove all backup files from the web root. Add web server rules to deny access to common backup file extensions.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Configuration File Exposed
remediation_brief: Remove configuration files from the web root immediately. Store configuration outside the document root. Rotate all exposed credentials.
description: A configuration file (e.g., .env, config.php, settings.py, database.yml) is publicly accessible. Configuration files typically contain database credentials, API keys, secret keys, and other sensitive values.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Remove configuration files from the web root immediately. Store configuration outside the document root. Rotate all exposed credentials.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Git Repository Exposed
remediation_brief: Immediately block access to .git directories via web server configuration. Rotate all credentials ever committed to the repository. Audit git history for secrets.
description: A .git directory or git repository index is accessible from the web root. An attacker can reconstruct the full source code, commit history, and any secrets ever committed.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Immediately block access to .git directories via web server configuration. Rotate all credentials ever committed to the repository. Audit git history for secrets.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: SVN/CVS Repository Exposed
remediation_brief: Block access to .svn and CVS directories via web server configuration. Remove version control directories from the web root.
description: A Subversion (.svn) or CVS repository directory is accessible from the web root. Repository metadata can be used to reconstruct source files.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Block access to .svn and CVS directories via web server configuration. Remove version control directories from the web root.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Log File Accessible
remediation_brief: Move log files outside the web root. Restrict access via web server configuration. Ensure log rotation is implemented.
description: An application or server log file is publicly accessible. Log files may contain IP addresses, usernames, session tokens, stack traces, and sensitive application data.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Move log files outside the web root. Restrict access via web server configuration. Ensure log rotation is implemented.

title: Database: Database File Exposed
remediation_brief: Remove all database files from the web root immediately. Store database files outside the document root and restrict filesystem permissions.
description: A database file (e.g., .sqlite, .db, .mdb) is directly accessible from the web server. This exposes the entire database contents to unauthenticated download.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Weak or missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access protected resources.
_x_remediation: Remove all database files from the web root immediately. Store database files outside the document root and restrict filesystem permissions.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS Certificate Expired
remediation_brief: Renew the TLS certificate immediately. Implement automated certificate renewal (e.g., Let's Encrypt with certbot or ACME protocol) to prevent future expirations.
description: The TLS certificate presented by the server has expired. Browser warnings will be displayed, and the certificate can no longer be trusted to guarantee the server's identity.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Renew the TLS certificate immediately. Implement automated certificate renewal (e.g., Let's Encrypt with certbot or ACME protocol) to prevent future expirations.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS Certificate Not Yet Valid
remediation_brief: Ensure server time is synchronized via NTP. Verify the certificate was issued correctly and replace if the issue persists.
description: The TLS certificate presented by the server has a notBefore date in the future, meaning it is not yet valid. Clients may reject the connection.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Ensure server time is synchronized via NTP. Verify the certificate was issued correctly and replace if the issue persists.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS Certificate Hostname Mismatch
remediation_brief: Obtain and install a certificate that matches the server's hostname. Use Subject Alternative Names (SANs) to cover all required hostnames.
description: The Common Name or Subject Alternative Names in the TLS certificate do not match the hostname being accessed. This breaks trust validation and may indicate a misconfiguration or MITM condition.
impact: A TLS certificate hostname mismatch indicates the certificate was not issued for the requested domain, causing browser warnings. Users who bypass these warnings become vulnerable to MITM attacks, and automated systems may silently accept invalid certificates.
_x_remediation: Obtain and install a certificate that matches the server's hostname. Use Subject Alternative Names (SANs) to cover all required hostnames.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS Certificate Self-Signed
remediation_brief: Replace the self-signed certificate with one issued by a trusted CA. Use Let's Encrypt for free, automatically renewed certificates.
description: The TLS certificate is self-signed and not issued by a trusted Certificate Authority. Clients cannot validate the server's identity, making the connection susceptible to MITM attacks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Replace the self-signed certificate with one issued by a trusted CA. Use Let's Encrypt for free, automatically renewed certificates.

title: Insecure Protocol Detected: Weak TLS Protocol Supported (SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS 1.0/TLS 1.1)
remediation_brief: Disable SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1. Configure the server to support only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
description: The server supports one or more deprecated TLS/SSL protocol versions (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, or TLS 1.1). These protocols have known cryptographic weaknesses exploitable by POODLE, BEAST, and similar attacks.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1. Configure the server to support only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

title: SSL/TLS Ciphers: Weak Cipher Suite Supported
remediation_brief: Configure the server to support only strong cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). Use Mozilla SSL Configuration Generator for recommended cipher lists.
description: The server supports weak cipher suites including NULL encryption, RC4, DES, 3DES, or export-grade ciphers. Weak ciphers can be exploited to decrypt TLS-protected traffic.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Configure the server to support only strong cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). Use Mozilla SSL Configuration Generator for recommended cipher lists.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS BEAST Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable TLS 1.0. Prefer TLS 1.2+ with GCM cipher suites. Enable server-side cipher preference.
description: The server is vulnerable to the BEAST (Browser Exploit Against SSL/TLS) attack due to the use of TLS 1.0 with CBC cipher suites. An attacker with network position can decrypt portions of encrypted traffic.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable TLS 1.0. Prefer TLS 1.2+ with GCM cipher suites. Enable server-side cipher preference.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS POODLE Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable SSLv3 entirely. Implement TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV to prevent protocol downgrade attacks.
description: The server supports SSLv3, making it vulnerable to the POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) attack. An attacker can force a downgrade to SSLv3 and decrypt session cookies.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable SSLv3 entirely. Implement TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV to prevent protocol downgrade attacks.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS DROWN Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable SSLv2 on all servers sharing the same private key. Regenerate private keys if SSLv2 was enabled.
description: The server supports SSLv2, making modern TLS connections vulnerable to the DROWN attack. An attacker can decrypt RSA-encrypted TLS sessions by exploiting SSLv2 export cipher weaknesses.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable SSLv2 on all servers sharing the same private key. Regenerate private keys if SSLv2 was enabled.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS HEARTBLEED Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Upgrade OpenSSL to 1.0.1g or later immediately. After patching, revoke and regenerate all TLS certificates and private keys. Invalidate all active sessions.
description: The server is running a version of OpenSSL vulnerable to Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160). An attacker can read up to 64KB of server memory per request, potentially extracting private keys, session tokens, and credentials.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Upgrade OpenSSL to 1.0.1g or later immediately. After patching, revoke and regenerate all TLS certificates and private keys. Invalidate all active sessions.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS LOGJAM Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable export-grade DHE cipher suites. Generate and configure strong (2048-bit or 4096-bit) DH parameters. Prefer ECDHE over DHE.
description: The server supports DHE key exchange with weak (export-grade) Diffie-Hellman parameters (512-bit), making it vulnerable to the LOGJAM downgrade attack.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable export-grade DHE cipher suites. Generate and configure strong (2048-bit or 4096-bit) DH parameters. Prefer ECDHE over DHE.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS FREAK Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable all EXPORT cipher suites. Update OpenSSL to a patched version. Enforce server-side cipher preference.
description: The server supports RSA_EXPORT cipher suites, making it vulnerable to the FREAK (Factoring RSA Export Keys) attack. An attacker can force the use of weak 512-bit RSA keys.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable all EXPORT cipher suites. Update OpenSSL to a patched version. Enforce server-side cipher preference.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS ROBOT Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable RSA key exchange cipher suites. Use ECDHE for forward secrecy. Patch the TLS library to a version with ROBOT mitigations.
description: The server is vulnerable to the ROBOT (Return Of Bleichenbacher's Oracle Threat) attack, allowing an attacker to perform RSA decryption and signing operations with the server's private key.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable RSA key exchange cipher suites. Use ECDHE for forward secrecy. Patch the TLS library to a version with ROBOT mitigations.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS CCS Injection Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Upgrade OpenSSL to 0.9.8za, 1.0.0m, or 1.0.1h or later. Restart the server after patching.
description: The server is vulnerable to the OpenSSL CCS Injection vulnerability (CVE-2014-0224). An attacker with MITM position can force the use of weak key material.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Upgrade OpenSSL to 0.9.8za, 1.0.0m, or 1.0.1h or later. Restart the server after patching.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS Ticketbleed Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Apply the vendor patch from F5. Disable TLS session tickets as a temporary mitigation.
description: The server is vulnerable to Ticketbleed (CVE-2016-9244) in F5 BIG-IP TLS implementations, allowing an attacker to read up to 31 bytes of uninitialized memory via TLS session tickets.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Apply the vendor patch from F5. Disable TLS session tickets as a temporary mitigation.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS SWEET32 Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Disable 3DES (TRIPLE_DES, 3DES_EDE) cipher suites. Prefer AES-GCM cipher suites.
description: The server supports 3DES cipher suites, making long-lived TLS connections vulnerable to the SWEET32 birthday attack, which can recover plaintext from encrypted traffic.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable 3DES (TRIPLE_DES, 3DES_EDE) cipher suites. Prefer AES-GCM cipher suites.

title: Missing Security Header: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Not Enforced
remediation_brief: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header with a max-age of at least 31536000 seconds (1 year), includeSubDomains, and preload directives.
description: The Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header is not present or has an insufficient max-age. Without HSTS, browsers may connect over HTTP, enabling SSL stripping attacks.
impact: Without HSTS enforcement, browsers permit plaintext HTTP connections, enabling SSL stripping attacks where an attacker downgrades the connection to intercept credentials and session tokens in transit.
_x_remediation: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header with a max-age of at least 31536000 seconds (1 year), includeSubDomains, and preload directives.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS Certificate Uses Weak Signature Algorithm (MD5/SHA-1)
remediation_brief: Replace the certificate with one using SHA-256 or stronger signature algorithm (SHA-2 family).
description: The TLS certificate is signed with a weak signature algorithm (MD5 or SHA-1). SHA-1 certificates are deprecated by major browsers and CAs, and MD5 certificates are cryptographically broken.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Replace the certificate with one using SHA-256 or stronger signature algorithm (SHA-2 family).

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS Certificate Short Key Length
remediation_brief: Replace the certificate with one using at least 2048-bit RSA keys, or preferably 4096-bit RSA or ECDSA P-256/P-384.
description: The TLS certificate uses an RSA key shorter than 2048 bits. Short RSA keys are susceptible to factoring attacks with sufficient computational resources.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Replace the certificate with one using at least 2048-bit RSA keys, or preferably 4096-bit RSA or ECDSA P-256/P-384.

title: DNS Vulnerability: Subdomain Takeover Vulnerability
remediation_brief: Remove dangling DNS records immediately. Claim or delete the referenced external resource. Implement DNS monitoring to detect future dangling records.
description: A subdomain DNS record points to an external service (e.g., GitHub Pages, S3, Heroku, Netlify) that is no longer claimed. An attacker can register the unclaimed resource and serve malicious content from the trusted subdomain.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Remove dangling DNS records immediately. Claim or delete the referenced external resource. Implement DNS monitoring to detect future dangling records.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Content-Security-Policy Header
remediation_brief: Implement a restrictive Content-Security-Policy header. Start with a report-only policy, monitor violations, then enforce. Avoid 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' directives.
description: The Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header is absent. Without CSP, the application has no defense against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks through browser-enforced policy.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Implement a restrictive Content-Security-Policy header. Start with a report-only policy, monitor violations, then enforce. Avoid 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' directives.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing X-Frame-Options Header
remediation_brief: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN'. Alternatively, use the CSP frame-ancestors directive.
description: The X-Frame-Options header is absent. Without this header, the page can be embedded in an iframe on any origin, enabling clickjacking attacks that trick users into performing unintended actions.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN'. Alternatively, use the CSP frame-ancestors directive.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
remediation_brief: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to all HTTP responses.
description: The X-Content-Type-Options header is absent. Without this header, browsers may perform MIME type sniffing, potentially executing uploaded files as scripts.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to all HTTP responses.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Referrer-Policy Header
remediation_brief: Add 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or a more restrictive policy to prevent sensitive URL data leakage.
description: The Referrer-Policy header is absent. Without this header, the browser's default behavior may leak the full URL (including query parameters and path) in the Referer header to third-party origins.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Add 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or a more restrictive policy to prevent sensitive URL data leakage.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Permissions-Policy Header
remediation_brief: Add a Permissions-Policy header that disables browser features not required by the application (e.g., camera, microphone, geolocation).
description: The Permissions-Policy (formerly Feature-Policy) header is absent. This header controls which browser features and APIs are available to the page and embedded third-party content.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Add a Permissions-Policy header that disables browser features not required by the application (e.g., camera, microphone, geolocation).

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Strict-Transport-Security Header
remediation_brief: Add 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload' to all HTTPS responses.
