title: Permissive Security Header: Insecure Content-Security-Policy (Unsafe-Inline Allowed)
remediation_brief: Replace 'unsafe-inline' with nonce-based or hash-based CSP. Refactor inline scripts to external files.
description: The Content-Security-Policy header contains 'unsafe-inline', which negates XSS protection by allowing inline JavaScript and CSS. This is the most common CSP misconfiguration.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Replace 'unsafe-inline' with nonce-based or hash-based CSP. Refactor inline scripts to external files.

title: Permissive Security Header: Insecure Content-Security-Policy (Wildcard Source)
remediation_brief: Replace wildcard sources with specific, trusted origin allowlists. Audit all third-party resource dependencies.
description: The Content-Security-Policy header contains a wildcard (*) source directive, allowing scripts or resources to be loaded from any origin. This effectively disables CSP's XSS protection.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Replace wildcard sources with specific, trusted origin allowlists. Audit all third-party resource dependencies.

title: Cookies: Missing Secure Flag
remediation_brief: Set the Secure flag on all session cookies. Ensure the application forces HTTPS for all authenticated requests.
description: One or more session cookies are set without the Secure flag. Without the Secure flag, the cookie will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, exposing session tokens to network interception.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Set the Secure flag on all session cookies. Ensure the application forces HTTPS for all authenticated requests.

title: Cookies: Missing HttpOnly Flag
remediation_brief: Set the HttpOnly flag on all session and authentication cookies to prevent JavaScript access.
description: One or more session cookies are set without the HttpOnly flag. Without HttpOnly, client-side JavaScript can read the cookie value, enabling session token theft via XSS.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Set the HttpOnly flag on all session and authentication cookies to prevent JavaScript access.

title: Cookies: Missing SameSite Attribute
remediation_brief: Set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax on all session cookies. Use SameSite=None only for legitimate cross-site cookie sharing, and always with Secure.
description: Session cookies are set without the SameSite attribute, or with SameSite=None without Secure. This enables Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks in browsers that do not implement SameSite by default.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax on all session cookies. Use SameSite=None only for legitimate cross-site cookie sharing, and always with Secure.

title: JWT: JWT Token in Local Storage
remediation_brief: Store JWTs in HttpOnly, Secure cookies instead of localStorage. This prevents JavaScript access and protects tokens from XSS-based theft.
description: JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) are stored in browser localStorage. localStorage is accessible to JavaScript, making JWT tokens vulnerable to theft via XSS attacks.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Store JWTs in HttpOnly, Secure cookies instead of localStorage. This prevents JavaScript access and protects tokens from XSS-based theft.

title: Authentication Bypass: JWT Algorithm Confusion (None Algorithm)
remediation_brief: Explicitly validate the JWT algorithm on the server side. Reject tokens with 'alg: none'. Use a strict allowlist of permitted algorithms.
description: The server accepts JWTs with the algorithm set to 'none', bypassing signature verification entirely. An attacker can forge arbitrary JWT payloads and impersonate any user.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Explicitly validate the JWT algorithm on the server side. Reject tokens with 'alg: none'. Use a strict allowlist of permitted algorithms.

title: JWT: JWT Algorithm Confusion (RS256 to HS256)
remediation_brief: Enforce algorithm validation server-side. Use separate code paths for asymmetric (RS256) and symmetric (HS256) verification. Never use the public key as an HMAC secret.
description: The server is vulnerable to JWT algorithm confusion. By changing the algorithm from RS256 to HS256 and signing the token with the public key as the HMAC secret, an attacker can forge valid JWTs.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Enforce algorithm validation server-side. Use separate code paths for asymmetric (RS256) and symmetric (HS256) verification. Never use the public key as an HMAC secret.

title: JWT: JWT Weak HMAC Secret
remediation_brief: Use a cryptographically random secret of at least 256 bits for HMAC-signed JWTs. Store the secret securely and rotate it periodically.
description: The JWT HMAC signing secret is weak or uses a common/guessable value. An attacker can brute-force the secret offline and forge arbitrary JWT tokens.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Use a cryptographically random secret of at least 256 bits for HMAC-signed JWTs. Store the secret securely and rotate it periodically.

title: JWT: JWT Signature Not Verified
remediation_brief: Ensure the JWT verification library is correctly configured to always verify the signature. Never decode without verification.
description: The server accepts JWTs with an invalid or tampered signature. The server is processing the JWT payload without verifying its integrity, allowing full token forgery.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Ensure the JWT verification library is correctly configured to always verify the signature. Never decode without verification.

title: Information Disclosure: JWT Sensitive Data in Payload
remediation_brief: Remove sensitive data from JWT payloads. Use JWE (JSON Web Encryption) if sensitive data must be embedded in tokens.
description: Sensitive data (e.g., passwords, PII, internal IDs) was found in the JWT payload. JWT payloads are base64-encoded but not encrypted, making them readable to any party with the token.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Remove sensitive data from JWT payloads. Use JWE (JSON Web Encryption) if sensitive data must be embedded in tokens.

title: JWT: JWT Token Accepted After Expiry
remediation_brief: Enforce 'exp' claim validation in JWT processing. Reject tokens with past expiration times. Use short token lifetimes with refresh token rotation.
description: The server accepts JWT tokens after their 'exp' (expiration) claim has passed. This allows indefinite reuse of stolen or leaked tokens.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Enforce 'exp' claim validation in JWT processing. Reject tokens with past expiration times. Use short token lifetimes with refresh token rotation.

title: Injection: JWT kid Header Injection
remediation_brief: Validate and sanitize the 'kid' header value. Use a whitelist of known key IDs. Never use the kid value directly in SQL queries or file system lookups.
description: The JWT 'kid' (Key ID) header parameter is used in an unsafe SQL query or file path lookup without validation. An attacker can inject a SQL payload or path traversal sequence into the kid header to manipulate key selection.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Validate and sanitize the 'kid' header value. Use a whitelist of known key IDs. Never use the kid value directly in SQL queries or file system lookups.

title: Injection: JWT jwk Header Injection
remediation_brief: Never trust keys embedded in the JWT header. Use only server-side trusted key stores for JWT verification. Ignore or reject tokens with 'jwk' or 'jku' headers unless explicitly required.
description: The server trusts the 'jwk' (JSON Web Key) header embedded in the JWT itself for signature verification. An attacker can embed their own public key in the jwk header and sign a forged token with the corresponding private key.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Never trust keys embedded in the JWT header. Use only server-side trusted key stores for JWT verification. Ignore or reject tokens with 'jwk' or 'jku' headers unless explicitly required.

impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Configure custom error pages. Remove all internal path references from HTTP responses. Review template and error handling code for inadvertent path disclosure.

title: Broken Access Control: Access Matrix — Unauthenticated Access to Authenticated Endpoint
remediation_brief: Implement authentication middleware that applies to all routes requiring login. Use a deny-by-default access control policy where routes must be explicitly marked as public.
description: An endpoint designated as requiring authentication is accessible without any session token or authentication credentials. Authentication enforcement is missing for this route.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Implement authentication middleware that applies to all routes requiring login. Use a deny-by-default access control policy where routes must be explicitly marked as public.

title: Broken Access Control: Access Matrix — Lower-Role Access to Higher-Role Endpoint
remediation_brief: Enforce role-based authorization on all privileged endpoints. Validate the user's role server-side on every request. Implement centralized authorization that cannot be bypassed.
description: An endpoint restricted to a higher-privileged role (admin, manager) is accessible by a lower-privileged authenticated user. Role-based access control enforcement is missing or inadequate for this endpoint.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Enforce role-based authorization on all privileged endpoints. Validate the user's role server-side on every request. Implement centralized authorization that cannot be bypassed.

title: Broken Access Control: Access Matrix — User A Can Read User B Data
remediation_brief: Validate object ownership on every read operation. Implement server-side checks that confirm the requesting user is authorized to view the specific object.
description: Authenticated user A can read data owned by user B by manipulating object identifiers in API requests. Object-level authorization is not enforced for read operations.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Validate object ownership on every read operation. Implement server-side checks that confirm the requesting user is authorized to view the specific object.

title: Broken Access Control: Access Matrix — User A Can Modify User B Data
remediation_brief: Validate object ownership on every write and delete operation. Require explicit ownership or permission grants before allowing modifications to another user's data.
description: Authenticated user A can modify or delete data owned by user B by manipulating object identifiers in API requests. Object-level authorization is not enforced for write operations.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Validate object ownership on every write and delete operation. Require explicit ownership or permission grants before allowing modifications to another user's data.

title: Broken Access Control: Access Matrix — Admin Functionality Accessible by Regular User
remediation_brief: Implement strict role-based access control with a separate administrative role. Enforce role checks at the API handler level for all administrative operations.
description: Administrative functions (user management, system configuration, data export) are accessible to regular authenticated users without elevated privileges. The access control matrix has gaps in administrative endpoint protection.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Implement strict role-based access control with a separate administrative role. Enforce role checks at the API handler level for all administrative operations.

title: Misconfigured Security Header: HTTP Security Header — X-Frame-Options Incorrectly Configured
remediation_brief: Set X-Frame-Options to 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'. Validate the header value is correctly parsed by target browsers.
description: The X-Frame-Options header is present but misconfigured (e.g., set to ALLOWALL or using an invalid value). An incorrect configuration may still allow the page to be framed, enabling clickjacking attacks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Set X-Frame-Options to 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'. Validate the header value is correctly parsed by target browsers.

title: Permissive Security Header: Content-Security-Policy — Unsafe-Eval Allowed
remediation_brief: Remove 'unsafe-eval' from the CSP. Refactor code that relies on eval() to use safer alternatives. Review all dynamic code execution patterns.
description: The Content-Security-Policy header contains 'unsafe-eval', which allows the use of eval(), setTimeout(), setInterval() with string arguments, and new Function(). This significantly weakens XSS protections.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Remove 'unsafe-eval' from the CSP. Refactor code that relies on eval() to use safer alternatives. Review all dynamic code execution patterns.

title: SSL/TLS Forward Secrecy: Not Supported
remediation_brief: Enable ECDHE (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral) cipher suites. Disable static RSA key exchange. Prefer ECDHE-RSA or ECDHE-ECDSA cipher suites.
description: The server does not support cipher suites that provide Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS). Without PFS, a compromise of the server's private key allows decryption of all previously captured TLS sessions.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Enable ECDHE (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral) cipher suites. Disable static RSA key exchange. Prefer ECDHE-RSA or ECDHE-ECDSA cipher suites.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLS OCSP Stapling Not Configured
remediation_brief: Enable OCSP stapling in the web server configuration (ssl_stapling on in Nginx; SSLUseStapling on in Apache). Include the OCSP stapling cache configuration.
description: OCSP stapling is not configured on the server. Without stapling, clients must query the OCSP responder directly to check certificate revocation status, introducing latency and potential privacy leakage.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Enable OCSP stapling in the web server configuration (ssl_stapling on in Nginx; SSLUseStapling on in Apache). Include the OCSP stapling cache configuration.

title: Injection: GraphQL SQL Injection via Argument
remediation_brief: Use parameterized queries or ORM methods in all GraphQL resolvers. Sanitize and validate all argument values. Apply input type constraints at the GraphQL schema level.
description: SQL injection was detected via GraphQL query arguments. Unsanitized argument values are passed to underlying database queries without parameterization.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Use parameterized queries or ORM methods in all GraphQL resolvers. Sanitize and validate all argument values. Apply input type constraints at the GraphQL schema level.

title: Information Disclosure: Sensitive Data in GET Request Parameters
remediation_brief: Transmit sensitive data via POST request bodies over HTTPS. Never include credentials, session tokens, or sensitive identifiers in URL query parameters.
description: Sensitive data (passwords, session tokens, personal information) is transmitted in GET request query parameters. GET parameters are logged in server logs, browser history, and Referer headers, exposing sensitive values.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Exposed information aids attacker reconnaissance and reveals sensitive system details.
_x_remediation: Transmit sensitive data via POST request bodies over HTTPS. Never include credentials, session tokens, or sensitive identifiers in URL query parameters.

title: Authentication: Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset
remediation_brief: Implement rate limiting on the password reset endpoint (per IP and per account). Add CAPTCHA after a threshold of requests.
description: The password reset endpoint does not enforce rate limiting. An attacker can repeatedly request password resets for target accounts, potentially triggering email flooding or token enumeration.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Implement rate limiting on the password reset endpoint (per IP and per account). Add CAPTCHA after a threshold of requests.

title: Authentication: Insecure Redirect After Authentication
remediation_brief: Validate post-login redirect URLs against a whitelist. Use relative paths for redirects. Never redirect to externally supplied URLs without validation.
description: The post-authentication redirect URL is controlled by a user-supplied parameter (e.g., next=, redirect=, returnUrl=) without validation. An attacker can craft a phishing URL that redirects users to a malicious site after successful login.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Validate post-login redirect URLs against a whitelist. Use relative paths for redirects. Never redirect to externally supplied URLs without validation.

title: Misconfigured Security Header: Lack of Security.txt File
remediation_brief: Create a security.txt file at /.well-known/security.txt specifying contact information, disclosure policy, and PGP keys for secure communications.

impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.

title: Web Vulnerability: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset Attack Exposure
remediation_brief: Apply patches from the web server vendor for CVE-2023-44487. Implement HTTP/2 stream limits and reset rate limiting. Update to a patched version of the HTTP/2 implementation.
description: The server supports HTTP/2 and may be vulnerable to the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset attack (CVE-2023-44487). An attacker can open and cancel streams at high speed to cause resource exhaustion and denial of service.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Network-level vulnerabilities may allow traffic interception, lateral movement, or unauthorized service access.
_x_remediation: Apply patches from the web server vendor for CVE-2023-44487. Implement HTTP/2 stream limits and reset rate limiting. Update to a patched version of the HTTP/2 implementation.

title: Discovery: CDN Active
remediation_brief: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Ensure security headers are set at the origin. Review CDN cache key configuration to prevent web cache poisoning.
description: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) was identified in front of the target via response headers or Server fingerprinting. TLS findings reflect the CDN edge configuration. Cache poisoning may be in scope. Header values and security posture may differ at the origin server.
impact: Active CDN detection reveals the content delivery and security infrastructure protecting the application. An attacker uses this to identify CDN-specific bypass techniques, origin server discovery methods, and CDN configuration weaknesses.

title: Discovery: WAF / Edge Security Platform Active

impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening.
_x_remediation: Keep WAF rule sets up to date covering OWASP Top 10 2025. Do not rely solely on WAF protection — fix underlying vulnerabilities. Review WAF bypass techniques relevant to the identified platform.

title: Discovery: WAF/CDN IP Block Detected
remediation_brief: Rotate scanner IP or use authorized IP whitelisting for the pentest engagement. Notify the client if the scanner is being rate-limited or blocked.
description: The WAF or CDN is blocking all requests from the scanner's IP address. All subsequent results from this point forward may be unreliable as every request returns a WAF block page.
impact: Detection of WAF/CDN IP ranges confirms that direct access to the origin server is mediated by a security proxy. An attacker targets CDN bypass techniques (IP history, DNS records, misconfigurations) to reach the unprotected origin.
_x_remediation: Rotate scanner IP or use authorized IP whitelisting for the pentest engagement. Notify the client if the scanner is being rate-limited or blocked.

title: Discovery: WAF/CDN Session Termination Detected
remediation_brief: Re-authenticate and resume the scan. Consider using static session tokens or IP-whitelisting for the scanner in the WAF configuration.
description: The WAF or CDN revoked the authenticated session mid-scan (HTTP 401 or login redirect returned on root URL probe). Authenticated scan results from this point may be incomplete.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening.
_x_remediation: Re-authenticate and resume the scan. Consider using static session tokens or IP-whitelisting for the scanner in the WAF configuration.

title: Discovery: WAF/CDN Challenge Page Active
remediation_brief: Request the client whitelist the scanner IP in the WAF configuration for the duration of the assessment.
description: The WAF or CDN is serving a JavaScript challenge or CAPTCHA page instead of real content. Automated probe results may be incomplete or inaccurate while the challenge is active.
impact: This finding provides informational context about the environment useful for security assessment and hardening.
_x_remediation: Request the client whitelist the scanner IP in the WAF configuration for the duration of the assessment.

title: Discovery: WAF Rate Limiting Detected
remediation_brief: If directory discovery is required, consider allowlisting the scanner IP in the WAF or load-balancer for the duration of the authorised engagement, or use a slower manual directory browsing approach.
description: The target or an upstream WAF/load-balancer is rate-limiting rapid sequential requests. A pre-flight burst probe detected that high-frequency requests degrade from the expected baseline response to 403/429/503 block responses. After 10 adaptive rate-down attempts the throttling persisted, indicating that the server enforces strict per-IP rate limits that prevent automated directory discovery tools from operating effectively.
impact: Automated directory discovery (feroxbuster) was skipped because every result would be a false-positive block response rather than a genuine 403 from the application. This means hidden directories, backup files, and administrative interfaces that would normally be discovered by recursive brute-forcing were not tested. The rate-limiting itself is a positive security control, but its presence should be documented as it affects assessment coverage.
_x_remediation: If directory discovery is required, consider allowlisting the scanner IP in the WAF or load-balancer for the duration of the authorised engagement, or use a slower manual directory browsing approach.

title: Authentication Bypass: Potential CDN Origin Bypass
remediation_brief: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Implement firewall rules to block direct internet access to the origin.

impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Implement firewall rules to block direct internet access to the origin.

title: Web Vulnerability: Web Cache Poisoning
remediation_brief: Ensure all headers that influence the response are included in the CDN cache key. Remove unkeyed header reflection from the application.
description: An unkeyed request header was reflected in a cached response. An attacker can inject this header with a malicious value and have the CDN serve that value to all subsequent users who receive the cached response.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Network-level vulnerabilities may allow traffic interception, lateral movement, or unauthorized service access.
_x_remediation: Ensure all headers that influence the response are included in the CDN cache key. Remove unkeyed header reflection from the application.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Expired
remediation_brief: Renew the certificate immediately and implement automated renewal (e.g., ACME/Let's Encrypt) to prevent future expiry.
description: The server's TLS certificate has passed its expiry date, causing browser trust errors and indicating a breakdown in certificate lifecycle management.
impact: An expired certificate causes browser warnings that train users to bypass security prompts, and in many configurations disables certificate pinning. An attacker can present their own certificate to users conditioned to click through warnings, enabling silent interception of all encrypted traffic.
_x_remediation: Renew the certificate immediately and implement automated renewal (e.g., ACME/Let's Encrypt) to prevent future expiry.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Hostname Mismatch
remediation_brief: Reissue the certificate to include the target hostname in the Subject Alternative Name extension.
description: The TLS certificate's Subject Alternative Names do not cover the target hostname. Clients will display a certificate mismatch warning, enabling trivial MITM attacks.
impact: A hostname mismatch indicates the certificate was issued for a different domain, causing browser warnings and potentially indicating a misconfigured or compromised service. Users who accept the mismatch become vulnerable to MITM attacks.
_x_remediation: Reissue the certificate to include the target hostname in the Subject Alternative Name extension.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Self-Signed
remediation_brief: Replace self-signed certificates with certificates issued by a trusted CA. Use ACME/Let's Encrypt for automated issuance.
description: The server presented a self-signed TLS certificate not anchored to a publicly trusted CA, preventing clients from verifying the server's identity and enabling trivial MITM attacks.
impact: Self-signed certificates are not validated by any trusted certificate authority, meaning clients cannot verify the server's identity. An attacker can trivially generate their own self-signed certificate and perform man-in-the-middle attacks without detection.
_x_remediation: Replace self-signed certificates with certificates issued by a trusted CA. Use ACME/Let's Encrypt for automated issuance.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Security Header
remediation_brief: Configure all recommended security headers: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.
description: One or more HTTP security headers are absent from the server response. Missing security headers weaken the browser's ability to enforce content security policies, prevent clickjacking, and mitigate XSS.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Configure all recommended security headers: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.

title: Permissive Security Header: Content-Security-Policy
remediation_brief: Replace permissive CSP directives with specific, trusted origins. Use nonces or hashes instead of 'unsafe-inline'.
description: The Content-Security-Policy header is present but contains permissive directives such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', or wildcard ('*') sources that significantly weaken its XSS protection.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Replace permissive CSP directives with specific, trusted origins. Use nonces or hashes instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

title: Permissive Security Header: X-Frame-Options
remediation_brief: Set X-Frame-Options to DENY or SAMEORIGIN. Prefer the frame-ancestors CSP directive for modern browsers.
description: The X-Frame-Options header is set to ALLOW-FROM or is absent, allowing the page to be embedded in iframes from arbitrary origins and enabling clickjacking attacks.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Set X-Frame-Options to DENY or SAMEORIGIN. Prefer the frame-ancestors CSP directive for modern browsers.

title: Permissive Security Header: Strict-Transport-Security
remediation_brief: Set HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year) and include the includeSubDomains directive. Consider adding to the HSTS preload list.
description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is present but has an insufficient max-age value or is missing the includeSubDomains directive.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Set HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year) and include the includeSubDomains directive. Consider adding to the HSTS preload list.

title: Permissive Security Header: Referrer-Policy
remediation_brief: Set Referrer-Policy to 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer'.
description: The Referrer-Policy header allows sensitive URL information to be included in the Referer header sent to third-party origins, potentially leaking authentication tokens or PII.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Set Referrer-Policy to 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer'.

title: Permissive Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options
remediation_brief: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.
description: The X-Content-Type-Options header is missing or set to a value other than 'nosniff', allowing browsers to MIME-sniff the content type and execute uploaded files as scripts.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.

title: Permissive Security Header: Cache-Control
remediation_brief: Set 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on all authenticated and sensitive pages.
description: Sensitive pages lack appropriate Cache-Control directives, allowing browser or proxy caches to store sensitive data. Cached sensitive pages may be retrieved by other users of shared devices.
impact: An attacker could use this information or weakness for reconnaissance or to facilitate more targeted attacks against the organization. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Set 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on all authenticated and sensitive pages.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Cache-Control on Sensitive Page

_x_remediation: Add 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' to all pages that display authenticated or sensitive data.

_x_remediation: Limit the number of operations allowed in a single GraphQL batch request. Apply per-operation rate limiting.

remediation_brief: Replace certificates with validity exceeding 398 days (Apple/browser-enforced limit). Ensure all certificates include Subject Alternative Names (SANs). Fix incomplete certificate chains by installing intermediate CA certificates. Automate certificate renewal with Let's Encrypt or ACME protocol. Use certificates with RSA-2048+ or ECDSA-256+ keys.

impact: Certificates signed with weak algorithms (SHA-1, MD5) are vulnerable to collision attacks that allow an attacker to forge a certificate with the same signature, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks that bypass certificate validation entirely.

description: fracture detected: Long Duration. This finding indicates a security concern that requires review.
impact: Excessively long TLS session lifetimes increase the window for session resumption attacks and reduce the effectiveness of forward secrecy. Compromised session tickets remain valid for the entire session duration.

title: Broken Access Control: BFLA: Role '{low_role}' Can Access Admin Path
remediation_brief: Implement server-side role-based access control checks on all administrative endpoints. Deny access for roles below the required privilege level and return 403 Forbidden.
description: A lower-privileged role can access an administrative endpoint that should be restricted to higher-privilege roles, indicating a Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA) vulnerability.
impact: An attacker with a low-privilege account can access administrative functionality, potentially managing users, configurations, or sensitive data beyond their intended authorization level.

title: SSL/TLS Ciphers: CBC Mode Cipher Suites Accepted
remediation_brief: Disable CBC-mode cipher suites on the server. Prefer AEAD ciphers such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.
description: The server accepts TLS cipher suites using Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode, which are vulnerable to padding oracle attacks such as BEAST and LUCKY13.
impact: An attacker may exploit CBC padding oracle vulnerabilities to decrypt TLS traffic or recover plaintext data from encrypted sessions.

title: SSL/TLS Forward Secrecy: Cipher Suites
remediation_brief: Configure the server to only accept cipher suites with forward secrecy (ECDHE or DHE key exchange). Disable static RSA key exchange.
description: The server accepts cipher suites that do not provide forward secrecy (e.g., RSA key exchange without ECDHE or DHE), meaning past sessions can be decrypted if the server's private key is compromised.
impact: If the server's private key is later compromised, all previously recorded TLS sessions using these cipher suites can be retroactively decrypted, exposing all historical encrypted communications.

title: Web Vulnerability: HTTP Request Smuggling — CL.0 Client-Side Desync
remediation_brief: Ensure all server components and reverse proxies consistently handle Content-Length headers. Disable HTTP/1.1 connection reuse where not required, or upgrade to HTTP/2 end-to-end.
description: The server is vulnerable to CL.0 client-side desync, a variant of HTTP request smuggling where the server ignores a Content-Length header on requests to specific endpoints, causing the connection to desynchronize.
impact: An attacker can poison the connection between a victim's browser and the server, hijacking subsequent requests to steal credentials, bypass access controls, or deliver malicious responses to other users.

title: Web Vulnerability: HTTP Request Smuggling — CL.TE Desync
remediation_brief: Ensure all servers in the chain use the same method to determine request boundaries. Configure the front-end to normalize ambiguous requests and reject those with both CL and TE headers.
description: The front-end server uses Content-Length while the back-end uses Transfer-Encoding, allowing an attacker to smuggle a second request within the body of the first.
impact: An attacker can bypass security controls, poison web caches, hijack other users' requests, or escalate privileges by injecting malicious requests that bypass the front-end proxy.

title: Web Vulnerability: HTTP Request Smuggling — TE Obfuscation Desync
remediation_brief: Reject requests with obfuscated Transfer-Encoding headers. Ensure all proxies and servers normalize and validate TE headers identically.
description: The server is vulnerable to Transfer-Encoding obfuscation, where variations of the TE header (e.g., extra whitespace, line folding, chunked1) cause front-end and back-end to disagree on request boundaries.
impact: An attacker can exploit TE header parsing differences to smuggle requests past the front-end, enabling cache poisoning, request hijacking, and access control bypass.

title: Web Vulnerability: HTTP Request Smuggling — TE.CL Desync
remediation_brief: Ensure all servers in the chain agree on request boundary determination. Configure back-end servers to prefer Transfer-Encoding over Content-Length, or reject ambiguous requests.
description: The front-end server uses Transfer-Encoding while the back-end uses Content-Length, allowing an attacker to smuggle a second request by manipulating chunked encoding boundaries.
impact: An attacker can bypass security controls, poison web caches, hijack other users' requests, or escalate privileges by injecting malicious requests past the front-end proxy.

title: Injection: Host-Header SSRF Surface ({label})
remediation_brief: Validate the Host header against an allowlist of expected hostnames. Do not use the Host header value in server-side URL construction or redirect logic.
description: The application reflects or acts upon the Host header value in server-side operations, creating a potential Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack surface via host header injection.
impact: An attacker can manipulate the Host header to redirect internal server requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure, potentially accessing internal services, exfiltrating data, or bypassing authentication mechanisms.

title: JWT: JWT Signing Secret Brute-Force Recovered ({alg})
remediation_brief: Use a cryptographically strong random secret (256+ bits of entropy) for HMAC-based JWT signing. Consider switching to asymmetric signing (RS256/ES256) where the private key never leaves the server.
description: The JWT signing secret was recovered through brute-force or dictionary attack, allowing an attacker to forge valid tokens with arbitrary claims.
impact: An attacker can create forged JWT tokens with elevated privileges, impersonate any user, bypass authentication entirely, and gain unauthorized access to all application functionality.

title: Discovery: Load Balancer Detected: {_lb_label}
remediation_brief: Suppress load balancer identification headers (e.g., Via, X-Served-By, X-Cache) in client-facing responses. This is informational and does not require immediate remediation.
description: A load balancer, CDN, or reverse proxy was detected in front of the target application based on response headers, cookies, or behavioral fingerprints.
impact: Knowledge of the load balancing infrastructure helps an attacker understand the network topology and may reveal vendor-specific vulnerabilities or bypass techniques for WAF/IDS systems.

title: Misconfigured Security Header: Missing Subresource Integrity — {entry['tag']} from {entry['host']}
owasp_web: A08:2025 Software and Data Integrity Failures
remediation_brief: Add integrity and crossorigin attributes to all <script> and <link> tags loading external resources. Generate SRI hashes using sha384 or sha512.
description: An HTML page loads a script or stylesheet from an external CDN or third-party host without a Subresource Integrity (SRI) hash attribute, allowing a compromised CDN to inject malicious code.
impact: If the external CDN is compromised, an attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript or CSS into pages that include the resource, enabling cross-site scripting, credential theft, or session hijacking for all users.

title: {_nik_title}
remediation_brief: Review the specific Nikto finding details and apply the recommended remediation for the identified vulnerability or misconfiguration.
description: A web server vulnerability or misconfiguration was identified by the Nikto scanner that does not map to a known Fracture finding category. The specific details are in the finding title.
impact: The specific impact depends on the vulnerability identified. Nikto findings typically indicate server misconfigurations, information disclosure, or known software vulnerabilities that could be exploited for unauthorized access or data exposure.

title: SSL/TLS Ciphers: Non-Standard Cipher Suites Accepted
remediation_brief: Configure the server to accept only well-known, IANA-registered cipher suites. Remove any experimental, vendor-specific, or non-standard cipher suites from the configuration.
description: The server accepts non-standard or experimental TLS cipher suites that may not have undergone the same level of cryptographic review as standard IANA-registered suites.
impact: Non-standard cipher suites may contain implementation flaws or use untested cryptographic constructions, potentially allowing an attacker to exploit weaknesses for traffic decryption or session compromise.

title: Injection: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) — POST Parameter
remediation_brief: Implement context-aware output encoding for all user-supplied data reflected in HTML responses. Use Content-Security-Policy to mitigate residual XSS risks.
description: A POST request parameter is reflected in the server's response without proper output encoding, allowing injection of malicious JavaScript that executes in the victim's browser context.
impact: An attacker can craft a malicious form submission that, when submitted by a victim, executes arbitrary JavaScript in their browser. This enables session hijacking, credential theft, account takeover, and delivery of malicious content.

title: SSL/TLS Ciphers: SHA-1 HMAC Cipher Suites Accepted
remediation_brief: Configure the server to prefer cipher suites using SHA-256 or SHA-384 for HMAC. Disable all SHA-1-based cipher suites.
description: The server accepts TLS cipher suites using SHA-1 for HMAC authentication. SHA-1 is considered cryptographically weak due to demonstrated collision attacks.
impact: While practical exploitation of SHA-1 HMAC in TLS is currently difficult, the use of SHA-1 does not meet modern cryptographic standards. Future attacks may make exploitation feasible, and compliance frameworks increasingly prohibit SHA-1.

title: SSL/TLS Forward Secrecy: {_tsf_id}
remediation_brief: Enable forward secrecy by configuring the server to use ECDHE or DHE key exchange exclusively. Disable static RSA key exchange and any cipher suites that do not provide forward secrecy.
description: A specific forward secrecy configuration issue was identified by testssl. The finding ID provides details on the exact cipher suite or key exchange mechanism lacking forward secrecy.
impact: Without forward secrecy, if the server's long-term private key is compromised at any point in the future, all previously recorded encrypted sessions using affected cipher suites can be retroactively decrypted.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: Lucky13 [UNCONFIRMED]
remediation_brief: Disable CBC-mode cipher suites and prefer AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). If CBC must be supported, ensure the TLS implementation includes constant-time MAC verification.
description: The server may be vulnerable to the LUCKY13 timing attack, a padding oracle attack against TLS CBC-mode cipher suites that exploits timing differences in MAC verification.
impact: A sophisticated attacker on the network path could potentially recover plaintext from TLS-encrypted sessions by measuring timing variations in the server's response to crafted ciphertext. The attack is theoretically possible but practically difficult to exploit.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: TLSv1.3 Not Supported
remediation_brief: Enable TLS 1.3 support on the server. Most modern web servers and load balancers support TLS 1.3 with a configuration change.
description: The server does not support TLS 1.3, the latest version of the Transport Layer Security protocol, which provides improved security and performance over TLS 1.2.
impact: Without TLS 1.3, the server lacks protections including mandatory forward secrecy, removal of legacy cipher suites, encrypted handshake, and 0-RTT resumption. Clients connecting with TLS 1.2 may use weaker cipher suites.

title: Out of Date Software: Vulnerable Component: {pname} {version}
remediation_brief: Update the identified component to the latest patched version. If an update is not available, evaluate compensating controls or consider replacing the component with a maintained alternative.
description: A third-party software component with known vulnerabilities was identified in the application's technology stack. The specific component name and version are in the finding title.
impact: Known vulnerabilities in third-party components can be exploited by attackers using publicly available exploit code. Impact ranges from information disclosure to remote code execution depending on the specific vulnerability.

title: Insecure Protocol Detected: {proto} Enabled
remediation_brief: Disable the deprecated protocol on the server and enforce TLS 1.2 as the minimum supported version, with TLS 1.3 preferred.
description: A deprecated or insecure protocol version is enabled on the server. The specific protocol (e.g., SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1) is identified in the finding title.
impact: Deprecated protocols contain known vulnerabilities (POODLE for SSLv3, BEAST for TLSv1.0) that allow attackers to decrypt encrypted traffic. Compliance frameworks universally prohibit these protocols.

title: Cookies: Cookie Prefix Violation: __Host-
description: A cookie using the __Host- prefix does not meet RFC 6265bis requirements (must have Secure flag, Path=/, no Domain attribute).
impact: An attacker may be able to set or overwrite the cookie from a subdomain or insecure context, bypassing the intended isolation guarantee.
remediation_brief: Ensure __Host- cookies include the Secure attribute, set Path=/, and omit the Domain attribute.

title: Cookies: Cookie Prefix Violation: __Secure-
description: A cookie using the __Secure- prefix is missing the Secure flag required by RFC 6265bis.
impact: The cookie may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, exposing its value to network attackers.
remediation_brief: Set the Secure attribute on all __Secure- prefixed cookies.

title: Missing Security Header: HSTS Not Preload-Ready
description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is present but does not meet browser preload list requirements.
impact: The site remains vulnerable to SSL-stripping on first visit until the HSTS header is received.
remediation_brief: Set max-age to at least 31536000 and add the includeSubDomains and preload directives.

title: Missing Security Header: Missing Cross-Origin Isolation Header: {header}
description: One or more cross-origin isolation headers (COOP, COEP, CORP) are not set.
impact: Without cross-origin isolation, the application may be susceptible to Spectre-class side-channel attacks or cross-origin information leaks.
remediation_brief: Set Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy headers as appropriate.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: JavaScript Source Map Exposed
description: A .js.map source map file is publicly accessible, exposing the original unminified source code.
impact: Attackers can read original variable names, comments, internal API endpoints, and business logic to find vulnerabilities.

mitre_attack.name: Gather Victim Host Information: Client Configurations

remediation_brief: Remove source map files from production deployments or restrict access to authenticated users.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Inline Source Map in JavaScript Bundle
description: A JavaScript bundle contains an inline sourceMappingURL data URI embedding the original source code.
impact: The full original source code is delivered to every visitor, exposing internal logic and potential secrets.
remediation_brief: Remove inline source maps from production builds; configure the build tool to exclude sourceMappingURL from output.

title: Misconfigured Security Header: Content-Type Confusion
description: The server responds with a Content-Type that does not match the requested Accept header without X-Content-Type-Options enforcement.
impact: Browsers may interpret content differently than intended, potentially enabling MIME sniffing attacks.
remediation_brief: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and ensure Content-Type headers accurately reflect response body format.

title: Injection: Server-Side Prototype Pollution
description: The application processes JSON input containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype properties, allowing modification of object prototypes.
impact: An attacker can inject properties into all JavaScript objects on the server, potentially achieving RCE, privilege escalation, or denial of service.
remediation_brief: Sanitize JSON input to strip __proto__ and constructor keys, or use Object.create(null) for parsed objects.

title: Injection: Potential Client-Side Prototype Pollution
description: JavaScript files use known prototype pollution sinks such as Object.assign, _.merge, or $.extend with user-controllable input.
impact: An attacker may be able to manipulate client-side object prototypes via URL parameters or form input, leading to XSS or logic bypass.
remediation_brief: Replace unsafe merge operations with Object.assign using Object.create(null) targets, or use libraries with prototype pollution protection.

title: Injection: Server-Side Include (SSI) Injection
description: The application processes SSI directives embedded in user input, allowing execution of server-side commands.
impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands on the server, read sensitive files, or include remote content.
remediation_brief: Disable SSI processing or sanitize all user input to remove SSI directive syntax.

title: Injection: Edge Side Include (ESI) Injection
description: The application reflects user input through an ESI-capable cache layer, allowing injection of ESI include directives.
impact: An attacker can perform SSRF through the cache layer, access internal services, or steal cached content from other users.
remediation_brief: Sanitize all user input to strip ESI tags, or disable ESI processing on the caching layer for user-controlled content.

title: Injection: Email Header Injection
description: A contact or email form accepts CRLF sequences in input fields, allowing injection of additional email headers.
impact: An attacker can inject Bcc/Cc headers to use the application as a spam relay, or modify email content for phishing.
remediation_brief: Strip or reject CRLF sequences in all fields used to construct email headers.

title: Authentication Bypass: Unicode Normalization Bypass in Authentication
description: The login form processes Unicode lookalike characters differently than expected, potentially mapping them to valid usernames.
impact: An attacker can bypass authentication controls by submitting visually similar Unicode characters that normalize to a valid account name.
remediation_brief: Apply Unicode NFKC normalization consistently before all authentication comparisons, and reject non-ASCII usernames if not expected.

title: Authentication: WebSocket Endpoint Missing Authentication
description: A WebSocket endpoint accepts upgrade requests without requiring authentication credentials.
impact: An attacker can connect to the WebSocket and access real-time data or perform actions without authenticating.
remediation_brief: Require authentication tokens or session cookies during the WebSocket upgrade handshake.

title: WebSocket: WebSocket Missing Origin Validation
description: A WebSocket endpoint accepts connections from arbitrary origins without validating the Origin header.
impact: An attacker can establish cross-site WebSocket connections from a malicious page, enabling cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
remediation_brief: Validate the Origin header during WebSocket upgrade and reject connections from untrusted origins.

title: WebSocket: WebSocket Message Injection (XSS)
description: The WebSocket endpoint reflects user-supplied message content without sanitization, enabling script injection.
impact: An attacker can inject malicious scripts through WebSocket messages that execute in other connected clients' browsers.
remediation_brief: Sanitize all WebSocket message content before rendering in the client, and implement server-side input validation.

title: Web Vulnerability: Web Cache Deception
description: Appending a static file extension to authenticated URLs causes the CDN/proxy to cache and serve sensitive content publicly.
impact: An attacker can trick users into visiting crafted URLs, causing their authenticated page content to be cached and retrievable by anyone.
remediation_brief: Configure the cache to respect Cache-Control headers and never cache responses based solely on URL extension; use Vary headers appropriately.

title: Web Vulnerability: OAuth redirect_uri Open Redirect
description: The OAuth authorization endpoint does not strictly validate the redirect_uri parameter, allowing redirection to attacker-controlled domains.
impact: An attacker can steal authorization codes or tokens by redirecting users to a malicious callback URL.
remediation_brief: Enforce exact-match validation of redirect_uri against pre-registered values.

title: Broken Access Control: OAuth Missing State Parameter (CSRF)
description: The OAuth authorization flow does not require or validate a state parameter for CSRF protection.
impact: An attacker can forge authorization requests and link their own OAuth account to a victim's session.
remediation_brief: Generate a cryptographically random state parameter per authorization request and validate it on the callback.

title: Information Disclosure: OAuth Token via URL
description: The OAuth implementation uses the implicit flow, placing access tokens in URL fragments.
impact: Access tokens can be stolen via browser history, proxy logs, or Referer header leakage to third-party resources.
remediation_brief: Migrate from the implicit flow to the authorization code flow with PKCE; never expose tokens in URLs.

title: Authentication: OAuth Scope Escalation
description: The OAuth authorization server grants elevated scopes beyond what the client originally requested.
impact: An attacker can obtain tokens with broader permissions than intended.
remediation_brief: Enforce strict scope validation on the authorization server; only grant explicitly requested and pre-approved scopes.

title: Authentication Bypass: MFA Bypass — Direct Navigation
description: Protected pages are accessible by direct URL navigation after initial authentication, bypassing the MFA verification step.
impact: An attacker who compromises a password can access the account without completing the second authentication factor.
remediation_brief: Enforce MFA completion as a server-side session state check on every protected endpoint, not just the login flow.

title: Authentication: MFA Missing Rate Limiting on OTP
description: The MFA verification endpoint does not enforce rate limiting on OTP submission attempts.
impact: An attacker can brute-force short OTP codes within the validity window to bypass MFA.
remediation_brief: Implement rate limiting and account lockout on the MFA verification endpoint after a small number of failed attempts.

title: Authentication: API Endpoint Missing Rate Limiting
description: An API endpoint does not enforce rate limiting, responding to 10 rapid requests without throttling.
impact: An attacker can abuse the endpoint for data enumeration, credential stuffing, or resource exhaustion.
remediation_brief: Implement rate limiting on all API endpoints using token bucket or sliding window algorithms.

title: GraphQL: GraphQL Alias-Based Batching
description: The GraphQL endpoint processes aliased duplicate queries in a single request, bypassing per-query rate limiting.
impact: An attacker can issue hundreds of queries in one request to enumerate data or bypass authentication rate limits.
remediation_brief: Implement query complexity analysis that counts aliases as separate operations, and enforce per-operation rate limits.

title: GraphQL: GraphQL Circular Fragment Accepted
description: The GraphQL endpoint accepts queries with circular fragment references that could cause infinite recursion.
impact: An attacker can craft queries with circular fragments to cause excessive server-side processing or crashes.
remediation_brief: Implement fragment cycle detection in the GraphQL query validator to reject circular references.

title: GraphQL: GraphQL Field Duplication Not Limited
description: The GraphQL endpoint processes queries with many duplicated fields without limiting the result set.
impact: An attacker can amplify response size by duplicating fields, potentially causing increased bandwidth usage.
remediation_brief: Implement query complexity limits that account for field duplication.

title: GraphQL: GraphQL Debug Extensions Exposed
description: The GraphQL response includes an extensions field containing debug information.
impact: Debug information reveals internal implementation details, query performance characteristics, and potential injection points.
remediation_brief: Disable GraphQL debug extensions in production environments.

title: Web Misconfiguration: HTTP/2 Cleartext Upgrade (h2c) Accepted
description: The server or reverse proxy accepts HTTP/2 cleartext upgrade requests.
impact: An attacker can use h2c smuggling to bypass proxy-level security controls, WAF rules, and access restrictions.
remediation_brief: Configure the reverse proxy to reject Upgrade: h2c requests or strip the header before forwarding.

title: Web Vulnerability: h2c Smuggling — Internal Endpoint Accessible
description: An internal endpoint that is blocked at the proxy level becomes accessible when requested via an h2c upgrade connection.
impact: An attacker can access admin panels, monitoring dashboards, or internal APIs by tunneling through the h2c upgrade.
remediation_brief: Block h2c upgrades at the reverse proxy and implement authentication on all internal endpoints regardless of network position.

title: Information Disclosure: Internal IP in HTTP Response
aliases: RFC 1918 Address Leakage in HTTP Response
description: The HTTP response body or headers contain one or more RFC 1918 private IP addresses (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), disclosing internal network topology.
impact: An attacker learns internal addressing, which aids lateral-movement planning, infrastructure mapping, and targeted exploitation of internal services.
remediation_brief: Remove internal IP addresses from HTTP response bodies, error messages, and headers. Configure application error handling to suppress internal details. Review proxy and load-balancer configurations to strip internal addresses from forwarded headers.

title: Information Disclosure: Application Responses Identify Valid Accounts
description: Login endpoint responses differ between valid and invalid usernames, allowing attackers to enumerate valid accounts through status codes, body length, error messages, or timing differences.
impact: An attacker can confirm which usernames exist in the system, enabling targeted credential attacks (brute force, credential stuffing) and social engineering.
remediation_brief: Return identical responses (status code, body length, content, and timing) for all login attempts regardless of whether the username exists. Use generic error messages like 'Invalid credentials'.

title: Unauthenticated Access: Authorization Gaps — Unauthenticated Access to Restricted Paths
aliases: Missing access control on admin paths
description: Administrative or restricted paths are accessible without authentication, indicating missing or misconfigured access controls.
impact: An attacker can access administrative functions, sensitive data, or configuration interfaces without valid credentials, potentially leading to full application compromise.
remediation_brief: Implement proper access controls on all administrative and restricted paths. Deny access by default and require authentication and appropriate authorization.

title: Injection: HTTP Parameter Pollution (Reflected)
description: Duplicate HTTP parameters are processed and reflected in responses, potentially allowing attackers to bypass input validation or inject malicious content.
impact: An attacker can inject a second parameter value that overrides or appends to the first, bypassing WAF rules, input filters, or business logic validation.
remediation_brief: Validate and reject duplicate parameters. Use framework-level parameter parsing that selects only the first occurrence. Encode all reflected user input.

title: Information Disclosure: Improper Error Handling — Server Error Exposed
description: Server returns HTTP 5xx error responses with detailed error information including stack traces, database errors, or debug output.
impact: Detailed error messages disclose implementation details (language, framework, file paths, database type, SQL queries) that aid targeted exploitation.
remediation_brief: Implement custom error pages that suppress stack traces. Disable debug mode in production. Log detailed errors server-side only.

title: Web Misconfiguration: Insecure HTTPS to HTTP Redirect Detected
description: Redirect chains downgrade from HTTPS to HTTP, exposing session tokens, credentials, and sensitive data to network-level interception.
impact: An attacker performing a man-in-the-middle attack can intercept credentials, session tokens, and sensitive data transmitted over the unencrypted HTTP connection.
remediation_brief: Ensure all redirects maintain HTTPS. Configure HSTS to prevent protocol downgrades. Review server redirect configurations.

title: Web Misconfiguration: Form Submits to HTTP from HTTPS Page
description: Forms on HTTPS pages submit data to HTTP endpoints, exposing form data (potentially including credentials) to network interception.
impact: Credentials or sensitive data submitted through the form travel over unencrypted HTTP, vulnerable to man-in-the-middle interception.
remediation_brief: Change all form action URLs to use HTTPS. Enable HSTS.

title: Information Disclosure: Internal Hostname in HTTP Response
description: HTTP response headers or body contain internal hostnames (.local, .internal, .corp, .lan, etc.), disclosing naming conventions and network topology.
impact: Internal hostnames reveal infrastructure naming patterns and topology, aiding reconnaissance and potentially enabling blind SSRF attacks when callback parameters exist.
remediation_brief: Remove internal hostnames from HTTP response headers (Server, Via, X-Powered-By, X-Backend-Server) and response bodies. Configure reverse proxies to strip internal routing headers.

title: Information Disclosure: Unhandled Application Exception Disclosed
description: HTTP responses contain exception class names, stack traces, or debug output patterns from various frameworks (Python, Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Ruby, SQL).
impact: Exception details disclose implementation language, framework version, file paths, database type, and SQL queries, significantly reducing the effort needed for targeted exploitation.
remediation_brief: Implement custom error pages. Disable debug mode in production. Log exceptions server-side only. Never expose stack traces in HTTP responses.

title: Discovery: Outdated or Unnecessary Website Detected
description: The website shows indicators of being outdated, abandoned, or unnecessary: old copyright dates, 'under construction' text, default CMS/server pages, or stale Last-Modified headers.
impact: Outdated or unnecessary websites expand the attack surface with unpatched software and forgotten configurations that are less likely to be monitored.
remediation_brief: Review whether this website is still needed. If not, decommission it. If needed, update its content and underlying software.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Log File Publicly Accessible
description: The web server exposes log file(s) to unauthenticated users. Log files commonly contain internal IP addresses, stack traces, usernames, session tokens, SQL queries, and file system paths. CWE-532, CWE-200.
impact: Attackers can harvest internal paths, database query patterns, user data, session tokens, and credentials from exposed log files. This information enables targeted exploitation of backend systems, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.
remediation_brief: Remove log files from web-accessible directories. Configure web servers to deny access to log file extensions (.log). Move log storage outside the document root. In Apache: <FilesMatch ".log$"> Require all denied </FilesMatch>. In nginx: location ~* \.log$ { deny all; }.

title: Authentication: Password Field With Autocomplete Enabled
description: Password input fields do not set autocomplete='off', allowing browsers to cache entered passwords.
impact: On shared workstations, cached passwords can be retrieved by subsequent users, compromising accounts.
remediation_brief: Set autocomplete='off' or autocomplete='new-password' on all password input fields.

title: Information Disclosure: Cloud Credentials in File
description: Cloud or CI/CD credential file(s) are accessible via the web, containing API keys, access tokens, database passwords, and service account credentials. Covers AWS credentials, Docker config, Kubernetes config, NPM config, Git credentials, and PostgreSQL password files. CWE-540, CWE-200.
impact: Attackers gain direct access to cloud infrastructure, container registries, Kubernetes clusters, or package repositories using the disclosed credentials. This enables data exfiltration, resource hijacking, supply chain attacks, and full infrastructure compromise.
remediation_brief: Immediately rotate all credentials found in exposed files. Remove credential files from the web-accessible directory. Add dot-files and credential paths to the web server deny list. Use IAM roles and managed identities instead of static credential files. Never store credential files in the document root.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Terraform State File Exposed
description: Terraform state file is accessible via the web, containing infrastructure secrets, API keys, database passwords, and complete cloud resource inventory.
impact: Full infrastructure credential compromise — database passwords, API keys, cloud resource details enabling lateral movement and data exfiltration.
remediation_brief: Store Terraform state in a secure remote backend (S3+DynamoDB, Terraform Cloud). Never serve state files via a web server.

title: Sensitive File Exposed: Sensitive Data Exposed in HTML Comments
description: HTML comments in page source contain sensitive keywords such as passwords, API keys, connection strings, or tokens.
impact: Credentials, API keys, or connection strings in HTML comments are visible to any user viewing page source, enabling direct account or service compromise.
remediation_brief: Remove sensitive data from HTML comments. Implement build processes that strip comments from production output. Conduct code reviews for comment hygiene.

title: Debug Endpoint Exposed: Laravel Ray Health Endpoint Exposed
description: Spatie Ray debug tool is accessible at /_ray/api/health. Ray allows remote code inspection and can expose application internals in production.
impact: Attackers can inspect application state, variables, queries, and stack traces through the Ray debug interface, gaining deep application knowledge for exploitation.
owasp_web: A09:2025 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: Remove Spatie Ray from production. Restrict debug tools to development environments only.

title: Debug Endpoint Exposed: Express.js Default Error Page
description: Express.js default error handler returns stack traces to clients, disclosing file paths, module versions, and application structure.
impact: Stack traces reveal internal file paths, module names, and line numbers that attackers use to plan targeted exploitation of known framework vulnerabilities.
owasp_web: A09:2025 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: Implement custom error handlers in Express.js. Set NODE_ENV=production to suppress stack traces. Never return error details to clients.

title: Information Disclosure: WebDAV PROPFIND Response Discloses Server Information
description: The server responds to unauthenticated PROPFIND requests with WebDAV property data, disclosing file metadata and directory structure.
impact: Attackers can enumerate server directory structure and file metadata without authentication, mapping the application for targeted attacks.
remediation_brief: Disable WebDAV on the web server unless required. Restrict PROPFIND to authenticated users. Block PROPFIND at the reverse proxy.

title: Web Misconfiguration: WebDAV Methods Enabled
description: The web server advertises WebDAV methods (PROPFIND, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, UNLOCK), enabling remote file manipulation capabilities.
impact: WebDAV methods can allow unauthenticated file upload, modification, or deletion. Historical vulnerabilities like CVE-2017-7269 demonstrate RCE risk.
remediation_brief: Disable WebDAV unless explicitly required. If required, enforce authentication and restrict to authorized users only.

title: Information Disclosure: Password Reset Token Exposed in URL
aliases: Reset Token in URL Query String
description: Password reset functionality includes the reset token in URL query parameters, exposing it in logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
impact: Reset tokens in URLs can be harvested from server logs, proxy caches, browser history, and Referer headers, enabling account takeover.
remediation_brief: Transmit reset tokens via POST body or HTTP headers, not URL query parameters. Implement short-lived, single-use tokens.

title: Information Disclosure: ETag
description: The ETag response header follows the Apache inode-size-mtime format, disclosing filesystem inode numbers that can fingerprint shared hosting.
impact: Inode values reveal file identity and can be used to detect shared hosting, map filesystem structure, and fingerprint specific web servers.
remediation_brief: Configure Apache: FileETag MTime Size (remove INode). For nginx, ETag is based on modification time and size by default.

title: Information Disclosure: Internal Hostname in SAN
description: The TLS certificate's Subject Alternative Names include internal hostnames that disclose naming conventions and network topology.
impact: Internal hostnames in certificates reveal naming conventions, infrastructure topology, and internal service locations to external attackers.
remediation_brief: Issue separate certificates for internal and external services. Remove internal hostnames from externally visible certificate SANs.

title: Information Disclosure: Cloud Storage Bucket URL Exposed
description: Cloud storage bucket URLs (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob) are exposed in page content, enabling cloud infrastructure reconnaissance.
impact: Exposed bucket URLs enable attackers to test for misconfigured public access, potentially accessing sensitive data stored in the cloud.
remediation_brief: Serve static assets through a CDN with a custom domain. Restrict bucket access policies. Do not store sensitive data in publicly referenced buckets.

title: Debug Endpoint Exposed: Laravel Ignition Execute-Solution Exposed
description: Laravel Ignition execute-solution endpoint is accessible, potentially enabling remote code execution via CVE-2021-3129.
impact: CVE-2021-3129 allows unauthenticated RCE through the Ignition execute-solution endpoint by chaining log file manipulation with PHP deserialization.
owasp_web: A09:2025 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
remediation_brief: Upgrade Laravel Ignition to a patched version. Remove debug tools from production. Set APP_DEBUG=false.

title: Web Misconfiguration: Unsafe Methods Enabled
description: The server advertises potentially dangerous HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, TRACE, PATCH, WebDAV) via OPTIONS that may allow file manipulation or cross-site tracing.
impact: Unsafe methods can enable file upload (PUT), deletion (DELETE), cross-site tracing (TRACE), or remote file manipulation (WebDAV), depending on server configuration.
remediation_brief: Disable unnecessary HTTP methods in web server configuration. Only allow GET, POST, HEAD, and OPTIONS. Restrict WebDAV methods unless explicitly required.

title: Permissive Security Header: Overly Permissive Permissions-Policy Header
description: The Permissions-Policy (or Feature-Policy) header grants wildcard (*) access to sensitive browser features such as camera, microphone, geolocation, or payment. This allows any third-party iframe or embedded content to access these device capabilities, increasing the risk of privacy violations and data exfiltration. CWE-16.
impact: Third-party content embedded in iframes can access the user's camera, microphone, geolocation, or payment APIs without restriction. A compromised or malicious third-party script can silently activate these features for surveillance or data theft.
remediation_brief: Restrict sensitive features in the Permissions-Policy header to self only or disable them entirely. Replace wildcard (*) values with specific origins or empty allowlists: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=().

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Expired TLS Certificate Detected
description: The TLS certificate presented by the server has passed its notAfter date and is no longer valid. Expired certificates break trust chain validation and cause browser warnings, which train users to bypass security prompts. An expired certificate may also indicate a forgotten or unmaintained service.
impact: Users encounter certificate warnings and may click through them, normalizing the bypass of TLS trust validation. An attacker could perform a man-in-the-middle attack more easily when users are conditioned to ignore certificate errors. The expired certificate may also indicate the service is unmaintained and potentially vulnerable.
remediation_brief: Renew the TLS certificate immediately through the issuing Certificate Authority. Configure automated certificate renewal (e.g. via certbot/ACME) and monitoring alerts for certificates approaching expiration.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Self-Signed TLS Certificate
