EternalBlue (CVE-2017-0144) allows unauthenticated remote code execution with SYSTEM privileges on unpatched Windows hosts.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Network-level vulnerabilities may allow traffic interception, lateral movement, or unauthorized service access.
_x_remediation: Apply MS17-010 immediately. Disable SMBv1: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false. Validate patch status using the Metasploit auxiliary scanner (auxiliary/scanner/smb/smb_ms17_010) for definitive confirmation. Isolate host until patched.

title: SMB Vulnerability: SMBv1 Protocol Enabled (EternalBlue Risk)
remediation_brief: Disable SMBv1 via Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Lanman Workstation > Enable insecure guest logons: Disabled) or PowerShell: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol. Verify with: Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol.
description: The SMBv1 protocol is enabled on this host. SMBv1 is a legacy protocol deprecated by Microsoft in 2014 that contains the vulnerability class exploited by EternalBlue (MS17-010). Even if MS17-010 is patched, SMBv1 contains additional weaknesses including susceptibility to NTLM relay attacks and other protocol-level vulnerabilities. Microsoft recommends disabling SMBv1 entirely on all systems regardless of patch level.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Disable SMBv1 via Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Lanman Workstation > Enable insecure guest logons: Disabled) or PowerShell: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol. Verify with: Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol.

title: Authentication Bypass: IPMI 2.0 Cipher Suite 0 — Authentication Bypass and Hash Capture
aliases: IPMI 2.0 Cipher Suite 0 — Authentication Bypass and Hash Capture
IPMI Cipher Suite 0 Auth Bypass Confirmed
remediation_brief: Disable IPMI Cipher Suite 0 in BMC configuration. Update BMC firmware to the latest version from the vendor. Restrict IPMI access (UDP 623) to dedicated out-of-band management VLANs with strict ACLs. Change all IPMI passwords to long, randomly generated values.
description: The IPMI 2.0 implementation on this host accepts Cipher Suite 0 (null authentication), allowing an unauthenticated attacker to authenticate to the BMC with any password (CVE-2013-4786). Additionally, the IPMI 2.0 RAKP protocol leaks a salted SHA1 or MD5 hash of the remote management password during the authentication handshake, enabling offline password cracking even when Cipher Suite 0 is disabled. Successful exploitation grants full out-of-band server management access including console, power control, and firmware update capabilities.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems.
_x_remediation: Disable IPMI Cipher Suite 0 in BMC configuration. Update BMC firmware to the latest version from the vendor. Restrict IPMI access (UDP 623) to dedicated out-of-band management VLANs with strict ACLs. Change all IPMI passwords to long, randomly generated values.

title: SSH Vulnerability: SSHv1 Protocol Supported
remediation_brief: Disable SSHv1 in the sshd configuration: set 'Protocol 2' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Restart the SSH service. Verify with: ssh -1 <host> to confirm SSHv1 is rejected.
description: The SSH server on this host advertises support for the SSHv1 protocol. SSHv1 is cryptographically broken and contains fundamental design flaws including the ability to insert arbitrary data into SSH sessions and an information disclosure vulnerability in RSA key exchange. SSHv1 has been deprecated since 2006 and its use undermines the integrity and confidentiality guarantees of the SSH channel.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Disable SSHv1 in the sshd configuration: set 'Protocol 2' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Restart the SSH service. Verify with: ssh -1 <host> to confirm SSHv1 is rejected.

title: SSH Vulnerability: 'none' Authentication Accepted (libSSH Bypass CVE-2018-10933)
aliases: SSH Vulnerability: 'none' Authentication Accepted (libSSH Bypass CVE-2018-10933)
remediation_brief: Upgrade libSSH to version 0.7.6 or 0.8.4 or later. For systems using OpenSSH this vulnerability does not apply — verify the SSH daemon in use. Apply vendor-supplied security patches immediately.
description: The SSH server accepts the 'none' authentication method due to an authentication bypass vulnerability in libSSH (CVE-2018-10933). An attacker can send an SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS message before authentication is complete, causing the server to grant full authenticated access without any valid credentials. This affects libSSH versions 0.6.0 through 0.7.5 and 0.8.0 through 0.8.3 and provides complete unauthenticated shell access to any account.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Unpatched software contains known vulnerabilities with potentially available exploit code.
_x_remediation: Upgrade libSSH to version 0.7.6 or 0.8.4 or later. For systems using OpenSSH this vulnerability does not apply — verify the SSH daemon in use. Apply vendor-supplied security patches immediately.

title: SSH Vulnerability: Weak/Deprecated Cryptographic Algorithms
remediation_brief: Update the SSH server configuration to restrict offered algorithms. In /etc/ssh/sshd_config set: Ciphers aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com; MACs hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com; KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512.
description: The SSH server advertises support for deprecated or weak cryptographic algorithms in its key exchange, host key, cipher, or MAC algorithm list. This includes algorithms such as arcfour (RC4), 3des-cbc, blowfish-cbc, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1, hmac-md5, and hmac-sha1-96. Use of these algorithms exposes SSH sessions to potential cryptographic attacks and violates current NIST and vendor security guidance.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Update the SSH server configuration to restrict offered algorithms. In /etc/ssh/sshd_config set: Ciphers aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com; MACs hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com; KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512.

title: RDP: RDP Without NLA (BlueKeep) (MS12-020)
aliases: RDP Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) — BlueKeep Exposure
RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
remediation_brief: Apply Microsoft security bulletin MS12-020. Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) as a compensating control. Restrict RDP access to authorised management networks. Block port 3389 at the perimeter firewall.
description: The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) service on this host appears vulnerable to MS12-020, which includes CVE-2012-0152 (denial of service via specially crafted RDP packet sequence) and CVE-2012-0002 (pre-authentication remote code execution via malformed RDP packet). CVE-2012-0002 is a pre-authentication memory corruption vulnerability affecting the Remote Desktop Protocol in Windows XP through Server 2008 R2. Exploitation can cause a crash (BSOD) or potentially allow arbitrary code execution.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Apply Microsoft security bulletin MS12-020. Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) as a compensating control. Restrict RDP access to authorised management networks. Block port 3389 at the perimeter firewall.

title: RDP: RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
aliases: RDP Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) — BlueKeep Exposure
RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
remediation_brief: Configure RDP to require TLS: set 'Security Layer' to 'SSL (TLS 1.0)' or higher in Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options). Enforce NLA. Apply a valid certificate to the RDP service.
description: The RDP service is configured with a low or incompatible security layer, or does not enforce strong encryption. Configurations using 'RDP Security Layer' (as opposed to 'TLS' or 'Negotiate with TLS') use RC4 encryption that is cryptographically weak and susceptible to session interception. This allows a network-positioned attacker to decrypt RDP session traffic and recover credentials or session data.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Configure RDP to require TLS: set 'Security Layer' to 'SSL (TLS 1.0)' or higher in Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options). Enforce NLA. Apply a valid certificate to the RDP service.

title: RDP: RDP Without NLA (BlueKeep) (MS12-020)
aliases: RDP Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) — BlueKeep Exposure
RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
remediation_brief: Enable NLA via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Require user authentication for remote connections by using NLA. Set to Enabled.
description: Network Level Authentication (NLA) is not enforced on the RDP service. Without NLA, unauthenticated network sessions are established before user credentials are validated, exposing the pre-authentication attack surface to vulnerabilities such as BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708) and DejaBlue (CVE-2019-1182). NLA moves authentication to the network transport layer, requiring credentials before a full RDP session is established.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Enable NLA via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Require user authentication for remote connections by using NLA. Set to Enabled.

title: Enumeration: NFS Export Points Enumerated — Potentially Unauthenticated Access
aliases: NFS Export Points Enumerated — Potentially Unauthenticated Access
remediation_brief: Audit /etc/exports and restrict each export to specific IP addresses or minimal CIDR ranges. Apply root_squash to all exports. Remove exports that are not required. Restrict showmount queries by blocking RPC portmapper (port 111) and NFS (port 2049) at the network boundary.
description: The NFS server responded to a showmount query and disclosed its export list. One or more exports are configured with overly permissive client specifications (e.g., wildcard '*', broad CIDR ranges, or no_root_squash), potentially allowing unauthenticated or minimally privileged network hosts to mount and access file system contents. Exposed NFS exports frequently contain sensitive data including SSH keys, configuration files, and application data.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Audit /etc/exports and restrict each export to specific IP addresses or minimal CIDR ranges. Apply root_squash to all exports. Remove exports that are not required. Restrict showmount queries by blocking RPC portmapper (port 111) and NFS (port 2049) at the network boundary.

title: Unauthenticated Access: NFS Directory Listing Accessible
aliases: NFS Export Points Enumerated — Potentially Unauthenticated Access
remediation_brief: Restrict NFS exports to specific authorised client IP addresses. Enable Kerberos authentication for NFS (sec=krb5p). Apply appropriate file permissions within the export. Consider migrating to SFTP or object storage for external file sharing.
description: An NFS-mounted export directory listing was successfully retrieved, confirming that the export can be mounted and browsed from the scanning host. The directory contents, file names, permissions, and modification timestamps are visible. This confirms NFS access is possible and that the export is not adequately restricted by client IP, user authentication, or Kerberos-based NFS (krb5 security flavour).
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Restrict NFS exports to specific authorised client IP addresses. Enable Kerberos authentication for NFS (sec=krb5p). Apply appropriate file permissions within the export. Consider migrating to SFTP or object storage for external file sharing.

title: Network Misconfiguration: SMTP Open Mail Relay Detected
remediation_brief: Configure the SMTP server to reject relay for domains it is not authoritative for. On Postfix: set mynetworks to trusted IP ranges only, configure smtpd_recipient_restrictions to reject_unauth_destination. On Sendmail: configure access DB to deny relaying. Implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
description: The SMTP server on this host will relay email for external domains, acting as an open mail relay. Open relays can be abused by spammers and phishing actors to send bulk email that appears to originate from the target organisation's IP space, damaging the organisation's email reputation, causing blacklisting, and potentially facilitating phishing campaigns. Open relays are identified by sending a test message from an external address to an external recipient via the server.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Security misconfigurations expose unnecessary attack surface or weaken defensive controls.
_x_remediation: Configure the SMTP server to reject relay for domains it is not authoritative for. On Postfix: set mynetworks to trusted IP ranges only, configure smtpd_recipient_restrictions to reject_unauth_destination. On Sendmail: configure access DB to deny relaying. Implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

title: Enumeration: SMTP User Enumeration Possible via VRFY
aliases: SMTP User Enumeration Possible via VRFY
remediation_brief: Disable the SMTP VRFY command. On Postfix: set disable_vrfy_command = yes in main.cf. On Exchange: VRFY is disabled by default but verify. Implement rate limiting and connection throttling on SMTP ports.
description: The SMTP server responds to VRFY (verify) commands, allowing an unauthenticated client to enumerate valid email addresses and usernames on the system. The VRFY command returns a 250 OK response for valid addresses and a 550 response for invalid ones. This provides an attacker with a list of valid accounts for targeted brute-force, phishing, or credential stuffing attacks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Disable the SMTP VRFY command. On Postfix: set disable_vrfy_command = yes in main.cf. On Exchange: VRFY is disabled by default but verify. Implement rate limiting and connection throttling on SMTP ports.

title: Enumeration: SIP Extension / User Enumeration
remediation_brief: Configure the SIP server (Asterisk, FreePBX, Cisco UCM) to return uniform error responses regardless of extension validity. Implement SIP authentication on all extensions. Apply rate limiting and IP blocking for repeated failed registrations. Restrict SIP access to known client networks.
description: The SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) service responds differently to OPTIONS or REGISTER requests for valid versus invalid extensions, enabling enumeration of valid user accounts and extensions. SVMap or a similar SIP scanner identified valid SIP usernames by observing differential server responses (200 OK vs 403 Forbidden vs 404 Not Found). Enumerated extensions can be targeted for brute-force authentication attacks to gain free VoIP calling or eavesdropping capabilities.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Configure the SIP server (Asterisk, FreePBX, Cisco UCM) to return uniform error responses regardless of extension validity. Implement SIP authentication on all extensions. Apply rate limiting and IP blocking for repeated failed registrations. Restrict SIP access to known client networks.

title: Web Misconfiguration: WebDAV Enabled
remediation_brief: Disable WebDAV if not required. If WebDAV is necessary, restrict it to authenticated users over HTTPS, limit access by IP, and audit PROPFIND and PUT/MKCOL method access in web server logs. On IIS: remove the WebDAV Publishing role feature. On Apache: remove the mod_dav and mod_dav_fs modules.
description: The web server has WebDAV (Web-based Distributed Authoring and Versioning) enabled. WebDAV extends HTTP with methods including PROPFIND, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, and DELETE. If write access is granted to unauthenticated or low-privileged users, an attacker can upload arbitrary files including web shells, leading to remote code execution. Even read-only WebDAV can disclose file system metadata and source code.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Disable WebDAV if not required. If WebDAV is necessary, restrict it to authenticated users over HTTPS, limit access by IP, and audit PROPFIND and PUT/MKCOL method access in web server logs. On IIS: remove the WebDAV Publishing role feature. On Apache: remove the mod_dav and mod_dav_fs modules.

title: Network Misconfiguration: JetDirect / PJL Printer Accessible
remediation_brief: Restrict access to port 9100 (JetDirect/RAW printing) using firewall ACLs to authorised print servers only. Disable PJL filesystem access commands in the printer administration console. Enable printer authentication and update firmware. Segment printers on a dedicated VLAN.
description: An HP JetDirect or compatible printer management interface (port 9100 / PJL) is accessible from the network. The Printer Job Language (PJL) protocol allows reading and writing the printer file system, retrieving print job history, changing configuration settings, and in some models extracting stored credentials. Unauthenticated access to PJL is a well-known attack vector against printers exposed on corporate networks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Restrict access to port 9100 (JetDirect/RAW printing) using firewall ACLs to authorised print servers only. Disable PJL filesystem access commands in the printer administration console. Enable printer authentication and update firmware. Segment printers on a dedicated VLAN.

title: Unauthenticated Access: Redis Unauthenticated Access
remediation_brief: Enable Redis authentication (requirepass) with a long randomly generated password. Bind Redis to localhost (bind 127.0.0.1) unless remote access is explicitly required. Use Redis 6+ ACL system to enforce per-user permissions. Block port 6379 at the network perimeter. Deploy Redis behind a VPN or bastion host.
description: The Redis server on this host is accessible without authentication. Redis provides no access control beyond an optional password, and when exposed without authentication, allows any connected client to read, overwrite, or delete the entire key-value store. Redis supports commands such as CONFIG SET that can be abused to write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations on the server filesystem, commonly used to achieve remote code execution via cron job or SSH authorized_keys injection.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Weak or missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access protected resources.
_x_remediation: Enable Redis authentication (requirepass) with a long randomly generated password. Bind Redis to localhost (bind 127.0.0.1) unless remote access is explicitly required. Use Redis 6+ ACL system to enforce per-user permissions. Block port 6379 at the network perimeter. Deploy Redis behind a VPN or bastion host.

title: Unauthenticated Access: MySQL Unauthenticated Access — Root with No Password
aliases: MySQL Unauthenticated Access — Root with No Password
remediation_brief: Assign a strong password to the MySQL root account: ALTER USER 'root'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'strong_password'; Revoke remote root access: DELETE FROM mysql.user WHERE User='root' AND Host!='localhost'; Bind MySQL to localhost or a specific management interface. Restrict remote access with GRANT statements limited to specific source IPs.
description: The MySQL server accepts connections as the root user without a password from the network. This grants an attacker full database administrator access including the ability to read, write, and delete any database, load/dump files to and from the server filesystem using LOAD DATA INFILE and SELECT INTO OUTFILE, and potentially execute OS commands via User-Defined Functions (UDFs). This represents complete compromise of database confidentiality and integrity.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Assign a strong password to the MySQL root account: ALTER USER 'root'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'strong_password'; Revoke remote root access: DELETE FROM mysql.user WHERE User='root' AND Host!='localhost'; Bind MySQL to localhost or a specific management interface. Restrict remote access with GRANT statements limited to specific source IPs.

title: Database: MySQL CVE-2012-2122 Authentication Bypass Risk
remediation_brief: Upgrade MySQL to a patched version (5.1.63+, 5.5.24+, 5.6.6+). Apply the vendor security patch. As a compensating control, restrict MySQL access by IP using GRANT statements and firewall rules.
description: The MySQL version detected on this host is potentially vulnerable to CVE-2012-2122, a memory comparison timing flaw in the authentication protocol. Due to a memcmp() optimisation in certain Linux builds and MySQL versions (5.1.x before 5.1.63, 5.5.x before 5.5.24, 5.6.x before 5.6.6), an attacker who sends the correct password approximately once in every 256 login attempts will bypass authentication. With repeated automated attempts, this allows authentication bypass for any known username including root.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Unpatched software contains known vulnerabilities with potentially available exploit code.
_x_remediation: Upgrade MySQL to a patched version (5.1.63+, 5.5.24+, 5.6.6+). Apply the vendor security patch. As a compensating control, restrict MySQL access by IP using GRANT statements and firewall rules.

title: Admin Endpoint Exposed: VMware ESXi
remediation_brief: Restrict ESXi management access (ports 443, 22, 902, 5900) to dedicated management VLANs and bastion hosts. Disable ESXi Shell and SSH when not in use. Apply VMware security advisories and vSphere patches immediately. Enable two-factor authentication via vCenter. Join hosts to vCenter and manage via RBAC rather than direct host access.
description: A VMware ESXi management interface (vSphere Client HTTPS on port 443, or ESXi Shell on port 22) is accessible from the network. ESXi hypervisors represent a critical attack surface: compromise of the hypervisor provides control over all guest virtual machines including the ability to power off, snapshot, clone, or extract disk images. ESXi has been a frequent ransomware target (ESXiArgs, Royal, BlackBasta), and exposed management interfaces are frequently exploited using known CVEs such as CVE-2021-22005 and CVE-2022-47966.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Restrict ESXi management access (ports 443, 22, 902, 5900) to dedicated management VLANs and bastion hosts. Disable ESXi Shell and SSH when not in use. Apply VMware security advisories and vSphere patches immediately. Enable two-factor authentication via vCenter. Join hosts to vCenter and manage via RBAC rather than direct host access.

title: RPC: RPC Null Session Permitted
remediation_brief: Restrict anonymous RPC access via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options: 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled. Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled.
description: The Windows RPC endpoint mapper accepts unauthenticated null session connections. A null session permits unauthenticated enumeration of shares, users, groups, and registry information via MS-RPC interfaces. This is frequently combined with SMB null session enumeration and forms a key component of unauthenticated Windows host reconnaissance, providing the attacker with Active Directory user account lists, group memberships, and domain SID information.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Restrict anonymous RPC access via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options: 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled. Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled.

title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Null Session Permitted
remediation_brief: Enable the following Group Policy settings: 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled; 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' = Enabled; 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled.
description: The SMB server permits null session connections — unauthenticated connections using an empty username and password. Via a null session, an attacker can enumerate share names, user accounts, group memberships, local policies, and domain SID information using tools such as enum4linux, rpcclient, or CrackMapExec. This information provides the reconnaissance foundation for subsequent targeted attacks including password spraying, credential brute-force, and Kerberoasting.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Enable the following Group Policy settings: 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled; 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' = Enabled; 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled.

title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Administrative Access via Credentials
aliases: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
remediation_brief: Rotate compromised credentials immediately. Implement LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) to randomise local administrator passwords per host. Disable the built-in administrator account. Enable SMB signing. Implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement pathways.
description: Valid credentials were used to authenticate to the SMB service with administrative privileges, and access to administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) was confirmed. Administrative SMB access allows reading and writing files anywhere on the target filesystem, remote service/registry manipulation, and is the primary mechanism used by post-exploitation frameworks (Impacket, CrackMapExec, Metasploit) for lateral movement and remote code execution via PsExec, WMIExec, or SMBExec.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Rotate compromised credentials immediately. Implement LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) to randomise local administrator passwords per host. Disable the built-in administrator account. Enable SMB signing. Implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement pathways.

title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
aliases: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
remediation_brief: Audit all SMB share permissions and apply least-privilege access controls. Remove write access from any accounts that do not require it for business purposes. Implement monitoring and alerting on new file creation events in sensitive shares. Enable SMB signing to prevent NTLM relay to share authentication.
description: An SMB share has been confirmed to be writable with the credentials used during the scan. Write access to a network share enables an attacker to plant malicious files, overwrite configuration data, introduce DLL hijacking payloads, or stage persistence mechanisms. If the share contains executable content served to other hosts, write access may lead to lateral movement or supply chain compromise within the organisation.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Audit all SMB share permissions and apply least-privilege access controls. Remove write access from any accounts that do not require it for business purposes. Implement monitoring and alerting on new file creation events in sensitive shares. Enable SMB signing to prevent NTLM relay to share authentication.

title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Share-Level Authentication (No User-Level Auth)
remediation_brief: Migrate to user-level SMB authentication. Configure the Windows workstation or server to use user-level access control: Computer > Properties > Sharing settings. Join the host to a domain and manage share access via domain user accounts and groups.
description: The SMB server is configured to use share-level authentication rather than user-level authentication. Under share-level authentication, access is controlled by a per-share password rather than user identity. This model lacks auditability (no per-user access logging), prevents granular access control, and is incompatible with modern SMB security features including SMB signing and SMBv2/3 message integrity. Share-level authentication is a legacy mechanism associated with Windows 9x/ME workgroups.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Migrate to user-level SMB authentication. Configure the Windows workstation or server to use user-level access control: Computer > Properties > Sharing settings. Join the host to a domain and manage share access via domain user accounts and groups.

title: Active Directory: BloodHound AD Graph Data Collected
aliases: BloodHound: Attack Path to Domain Admin Found
remediation_brief: Review the collected BloodHound data to identify and remediate high-risk attack paths (paths to Domain Admin, DCSync rights, unconstrained delegation). Implement tiered administration to limit exposure. Monitor LDAP query volume for anomalous bulk enumeration indicative of BloodHound collection.
description: BloodHound-Python successfully collected Active Directory object data including users, groups, computers, GPOs, OUs, and ACLs and produced graph database ingest files. This data enables graph-based analysis of Active Directory attack paths, privilege escalation routes, and delegation abuses. The collection itself demonstrates that the network is reachable from the attacker's position with sufficient credential access to query LDAP at the level required for BloodHound enumeration.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Review the collected BloodHound data to identify and remediate high-risk attack paths (paths to Domain Admin, DCSync rights, unconstrained delegation). Implement tiered administration to limit exposure. Monitor LDAP query volume for anomalous bulk enumeration indicative of BloodHound collection.

title: Enumeration: LDAP Domain Users Enumerated
remediation_brief: Implement LDAP query monitoring and alerting for bulk user enumeration. Apply Protected Users security group membership to privileged accounts. Enforce Kerberos-only authentication for sensitive accounts. Implement fine-grained password policies. Monitor for anomalous LDAP query patterns in Windows event logs (Event ID 4661).
description: LDAP enumeration successfully retrieved a list of domain user accounts from Active Directory. The enumerated data may include usernames, display names, email addresses, account status, last logon timestamps, and group memberships. This user list provides an attacker with a validated target list for password spraying, credential stuffing, phishing, and Kerberoasting attacks. Successful LDAP enumeration often requires only a low-privileged domain account.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems.
_x_remediation: Implement LDAP query monitoring and alerting for bulk user enumeration. Apply Protected Users security group membership to privileged accounts. Enforce Kerberos-only authentication for sensitive accounts. Implement fine-grained password policies. Monitor for anomalous LDAP query patterns in Windows event logs (Event ID 4661).

title: Enumeration: Valid Kerberos Usernames Enumerated
remediation_brief: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts to reduce the information disclosed in error responses. Monitor domain controller logs for unusual AS-REQ volume (Event IDs 4768, 4771). Deploy a SIEM alert for repeated KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN errors from a single source IP.
description: Kerbrute or a similar tool enumerated valid Active Directory usernames by sending AS-REQ messages and observing Kerberos error code differences: valid accounts return KRB5KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED (18) or KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED (12/18) while invalid accounts return KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN (6). This technique does not require any credentials and works even when null sessions are disabled, providing a validated username list for subsequent password spray or brute-force attacks.
impact: An attacker could potentially exploit this weakness to gain partial access, disclose sensitive information, or degrade the security posture of the affected system.
_x_remediation: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts to reduce the information disclosed in error responses. Monitor domain controller logs for unusual AS-REQ volume (Event IDs 4768, 4771). Deploy a SIEM alert for repeated KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN errors from a single source IP.

title: Authentication: Domain Accounts with Password Not Required
aliases: Domain Accounts with Password Not Required
remediation_brief: Identify all accounts with the PASSWD_NOTREQD flag set: Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNotRequired -eq $True}. Set a strong password on each account and remove the flag: Set-ADUser -Identity <user> -PasswordNotRequired $false. Audit and enforce the domain password policy.
description: One or more Active Directory user accounts have the PASSWD_NOTREQD (UF_PASSWD_NOTREQD, userAccountControl bit 0x0020) flag set, meaning the account may have an empty or blank password. Accounts with this flag are not subject to the domain password policy minimum length requirement and can be authenticated with an empty password. These accounts represent a trivially exploitable authentication bypass if empty passwords are present.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.
_x_remediation: Identify all accounts with the PASSWD_NOTREQD flag set: Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNotRequired -eq $True}. Set a strong password on each account and remove the flag: Set-ADUser -Identity <user> -PasswordNotRequired $false. Audit and enforce the domain password policy.

title: Active Directory: Privileged Domain Accounts Identified
aliases: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions

description: LDAP enumeration identified user accounts with membership in highly privileged Active Directory groups such as Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Backup Operators, or Account Operators. impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Improper access controls may allow privilege escalation or unauthorized resource access.

Add privileged accounts to the Protected Users security group. Enforce MFA for all administrative accounts. Restrict privileged account logon rights via GPO.

title: Web Vulnerability: WordPress Core Vulnerability

title: Insecure Protocol Detected: HTTP
aliases: Information Disclosure: Plaintext Credentials in Web Content
remediation_brief: Migrate the service to HTTPS with a valid TLS certificate. Configure HTTP to HTTPS redirection. Set the Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header with a long max-age value. Obtain a certificate from Let's Encrypt (free) or a commercial CA.
description: A web application or service is served over unencrypted HTTP. All data transmitted between the client and server including session cookies, form data, and credentials is transmitted in plaintext and can be intercepted by any network-positioned observer. Without HTTPS, the service is also susceptible to SSL stripping and man-in-the-middle content injection attacks.
impact: HTTP services transmit all data in plaintext, allowing any attacker with network access to passively intercept credentials, session tokens, API keys, and business data. Active MITM attackers can also inject malicious content, redirect authentication flows, and modify transactions in transit.
_x_remediation: Migrate the service to HTTPS with a valid TLS certificate. Configure HTTP to HTTPS redirection. Set the Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header with a long max-age value. Obtain a certificate from Let's Encrypt (free) or a commercial CA.

title: Deprecated Protocol Enabled
aliases: Information Disclosure: Plaintext Credentials in Web Content
remediation_brief: Disable the deprecated protocol and replace with a modern, secure alternative. Telnet: use SSH. SNMPv1/v2: use SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption. RIPv1: use RIPv2 or OSPF. Review all network service configurations for use of deprecated protocols.
description: A deprecated network protocol is enabled on this host. Deprecated protocols lack modern security controls including strong authentication and encryption, have known cryptographic weaknesses or design flaws, and are no longer maintained by their developers. Examples include Telnet, RSH, RLOGIN, SNMPv1/v2, RIPv1, and older versions of SMB. The specific protocol is recorded in the finding evidence.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Disable the deprecated protocol and replace with a modern, secure alternative. Telnet: use SSH. SNMPv1/v2: use SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption. RIPv1: use RIPv2 or OSPF. Review all network service configurations for use of deprecated protocols.

title: Information Disclosure: Plaintext Credentials in Web Content
aliases: Information Disclosure: Plaintext Credentials in Web Content
remediation_brief: Immediately rotate all exposed credentials. Remove credentials from web-accessible content. Use environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) for credential storage. Audit the web server document root for sensitive files. Implement web application firewall rules to prevent configuration file access.
description: Credentials (usernames, passwords, API keys, tokens, or connection strings) were discovered in plaintext within web-accessible content, including HTML source, JavaScript files, configuration files served by the web server, or directory listing contents. Plaintext credentials in web-accessible content can be harvested by any user who can access the page and frequently provide direct access to backend databases, APIs, or privileged service accounts.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Weak cryptographic implementations may allow interception, decryption, or forgery of protected communications.
_x_remediation: Immediately rotate all exposed credentials. Remove credentials from web-accessible content. Use environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) for credential storage. Audit the web server document root for sensitive files. Implement web application firewall rules to prevent configuration file access.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: BEAST
remediation_brief: Disable TLS 1.0 and SSLv3 entirely. Enable TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. Prioritise AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) which are not susceptible to BEAST. Modern TLS 1.2 with RC4 elimination and GCM prioritisation eliminates the BEAST attack surface.
description: The server is susceptible to the BEAST attack (Browser Exploit Against SSL/TLS, CVE-2011-3389). BEAST exploits a CBC mode initialisation vector (IV) predictability vulnerability in TLS 1.0 and earlier, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker who can inject chosen plaintext to decrypt CBC-encrypted session data. While the attack requires a network-adjacent attacker and active JavaScript injection in the victim's browser, TLS 1.0 should not be used in modern deployments.
impact: BEAST (Browser Exploit Against SSL/TLS) exploits a vulnerability in TLS 1.0's CBC-mode cipher initialization to decrypt HTTPS cookies and authentication tokens. An attacker with network access can inject chosen plaintext to recover session secrets, enabling session hijacking.
_x_remediation: Disable TLS 1.0 and SSLv3 entirely. Enable TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. Prioritise AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) which are not susceptible to BEAST. Modern TLS 1.2 with RC4 elimination and GCM prioritisation eliminates the BEAST attack surface.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: LUCKY13
remediation_brief: Prioritise and restrict TLS cipher suites to AEAD algorithms (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) which are immune to CBC padding oracle attacks. Disable all CBC mode cipher suites. Enable TLS 1.3 which exclusively uses AEAD ciphers.
description: The server supports CBC mode cipher suites with HMAC-SHA1 or HMAC-MD5, making it potentially susceptible to the LUCKY13 timing attack (CVE-2013-0169). LUCKY13 is a padding oracle attack against CBC-mode TLS that allows an attacker with precise network timing measurements to decrypt recorded TLS session data. The attack requires approximately 2^23 oracle queries per 16 bytes of plaintext decrypted and is primarily a theoretical concern but indicates use of non-AEAD cipher suites.
impact: LUCKY13 (CVE-2013-0169) is a timing side-channel attack against CBC-mode cipher suites in TLS. An attacker with network-level access can recover plaintext from encrypted sessions by measuring processing time differences.
_x_remediation: Prioritise and restrict TLS cipher suites to AEAD algorithms (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) which are immune to CBC padding oracle attacks. Disable all CBC mode cipher suites. Enable TLS 1.3 which exclusively uses AEAD ciphers.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: SWEET32
remediation_brief: Disable all 64-bit block cipher suites including 3DES (TRIPLE-DES, 3DES-EDE-CBC-SHA) and Blowfish. Ensure the server's cipher list does not include any cipher containing DES or 3DES. Enable only AES-128 and AES-256 based ciphers with GCM mode.
description: The server supports cipher suites using 64-bit block ciphers (Triple-DES/3DES or Blowfish), making it susceptible to the SWEET32 birthday attack (CVE-2016-2183). After approximately 2^32 blocks (about 32 GB of traffic), an attacker capturing a long-lived TLS session can exploit birthday bound collisions in the CBC mode to recover short, repeated plaintext segments such as HTTP cookies. 3DES-based cipher suites (TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA) should be considered deprecated.
impact: SWEET32 exploits the birthday bound weakness in 64-bit block ciphers (3DES, Blowfish) used in TLS. After capturing approximately 32GB of ciphertext from a long-lived session, an attacker can recover plaintext blocks, potentially exposing session cookies and authentication tokens.
_x_remediation: Disable all 64-bit block cipher suites including 3DES (TRIPLE-DES, 3DES-EDE-CBC-SHA) and Blowfish. Ensure the server's cipher list does not include any cipher containing DES or 3DES. Enable only AES-128 and AES-256 based ciphers with GCM mode.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Chain Incomplete
remediation_brief: Reconfigure the TLS server to present the full certificate chain including all required intermediate CA certificates. Obtain the intermediate certificates from the issuing CA and concatenate them with the server certificate in the correct order (leaf first, then intermediates). Verify with: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -showcerts.
description: The TLS server does not present the full certificate chain during the TLS handshake, omitting one or more intermediate CA certificates. Clients that do not have the intermediate certificate pre-cached will be unable to build a trusted chain to the root CA and will display a certificate error. This indicates a misconfiguration in the server's TLS certificate installation. Some strict clients and mobile browsers do not perform intermediate certificate fetching (AIA chasing) and will fail validation.
impact: An incomplete certificate chain prevents clients from validating the certificate's trust path. Some clients may reject the connection outright, while others silently proceed without full validation, creating inconsistent security posture across the user base.
_x_remediation: Reconfigure the TLS server to present the full certificate chain including all required intermediate CA certificates. Obtain the intermediate certificates from the issuing CA and concatenate them with the server certificate in the correct order (leaf first, then intermediates). Verify with: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -showcerts.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Long Duration
remediation_brief: Replace the certificate with one having a validity period of 398 days or less. Configure automated certificate renewal (ACME/Let's Encrypt or vendor auto-renewal) to ensure certificates are routinely replaced before expiry. For new certificates, request 90-day validity where possible.
description: The TLS certificate has a validity period exceeding 398 days (approximately 13 months). Since September 2020, Apple, Google, and Mozilla enforce a maximum certificate validity of 398 days, and certificates with longer lifetimes will be rejected by current versions of Safari, Chrome, and Firefox. Longer validity periods also increase the exposure window if a private key is compromised, as the certificate cannot be superseded until it expires or is revoked.
impact: Long-lived certificates increase the window of exposure if the private key is compromised. Industry best practice limits certificate lifetime to reduce the impact of key compromise and ensure regular rotation of cryptographic material.
_x_remediation: Replace the certificate with one having a validity period of 398 days or less. Configure automated certificate renewal (ACME/Let's Encrypt or vendor auto-renewal) to ensure certificates are routinely replaced before expiry. For new certificates, request 90-day validity where possible.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Missing SAN
remediation_brief: Replace the certificate with one that includes a valid Subject Alternative Name (SAN) extension containing the intended hostname(s). All modern CAs issue certificates with SAN by default. If using an internal CA, update the certificate template to include the SAN extension.
description: The TLS certificate does not contain a Subject Alternative Name (SAN) extension. Since 2017, all major browsers require a SAN to be present and have deprecated reliance on the Common Name (CN) field for hostname validation. Certificates without a SAN will cause certificate validation errors in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari for any hostname validation, even if the CN matches. This is a certificate issuance and lifecycle management deficiency.
impact: A certificate without Subject Alternative Names (SAN) relies solely on the Common Name field for hostname validation. Modern browsers require SAN entries and may reject CN-only certificates, causing service interruptions and security warnings.
_x_remediation: Replace the certificate with one that includes a valid Subject Alternative Name (SAN) extension containing the intended hostname(s). All modern CAs issue certificates with SAN by default. If using an internal CA, update the certificate template to include the SAN extension.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Serial Number Entropy

mitre_attack.name: Search Open Technical Databases: Digital Certificates

remediation_brief: Replace the certificate if issued by an internal CA with an outdated serial number generation algorithm. Update the internal CA software or configuration to generate serial numbers with at least 64 bits of CSPRNG-sourced entropy. For externally issued certificates, verify the CA is CA/B Forum compliant.
description: The TLS certificate serial number has low entropy, suggesting it was generated with a non-random or predictable serial number algorithm. CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements (Section 7.1) require that certificate serial numbers contain at least 64 bits of unpredictable entropy. Low-entropy serial numbers may indicate an outdated certificate authority or CA software configuration, and in conjunction with other weaknesses can facilitate certificate collision or impersonation attacks.
impact: Low entropy in certificate serial numbers indicates weak random number generation in the issuing CA's infrastructure. This can enable serial number prediction attacks that facilitate certificate forgery.
_x_remediation: Replace the certificate if issued by an internal CA with an outdated serial number generation algorithm. Update the internal CA software or configuration to generate serial numbers with at least 64 bits of CSPRNG-sourced entropy. For externally issued certificates, verify the CA is CA/B Forum compliant.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Weak Encryption Method
remediation_brief: Replace the certificate with one using SHA-256 (or stronger) as the signature algorithm and at minimum RSA-2048 or ECDSA P-256 for the public key. Verify the replacement certificate: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text | grep 'Signature Algorithm'.
description: The TLS certificate uses a weak signature algorithm or public key. This includes SHA-1 signed certificates (deprecated since 2017), RSA keys shorter than 2048 bits, DSA keys shorter than 2048 bits, or Elliptic Curve keys shorter than 224 bits. Certificates signed with SHA-1 are vulnerable to chosen-prefix collision attacks (demonstrated by SHAttered). Certificates with short RSA keys are vulnerable to factorisation attacks given current computational resources.
impact: Certificates signed with weak algorithms (SHA-1, MD5) are vulnerable to collision attacks that allow an attacker to forge a certificate with the same signature, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks that bypass certificate validation entirely.
_x_remediation: Replace the certificate with one using SHA-256 (or stronger) as the signature algorithm and at minimum RSA-2048 or ECDSA P-256 for the public key. Verify the replacement certificate: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text | grep 'Signature Algorithm'.

title: SSL/TLS Session: Long Duration
aliases: SSL/TLS Cipher: No Cipher Order Configured
remediation_brief: Reduce TLS session ticket lifetime to a maximum of 24 hours. Rotate TLS session ticket encryption keys regularly (every 6-12 hours). Set the session cache timeout to a reasonable value. On nginx: ssl_session_timeout 1h; ssl_session_ticket_key rotation should be automated.
description: The TLS server allows session resumption with a session ticket lifetime or session cache timeout exceeding recommended limits (typically more than 24 hours for session tickets or more than 10 hours for session IDs). Long-lived TLS sessions extend the window during which a stolen session ticket or cached session key can be replayed by an attacker to resume a session without re-authenticating. This also limits the effectiveness of forward secrecy when session tickets are encrypted with a long-lived key.
impact: Excessively long TLS session lifetimes increase the window for session resumption attacks and reduce the effectiveness of forward secrecy. Compromised session tickets remain valid for the entire session duration.
_x_remediation: Reduce TLS session ticket lifetime to a maximum of 24 hours. Rotate TLS session ticket encryption keys regularly (every 6-12 hours). Set the session cache timeout to a reasonable value. On nginx: ssl_session_timeout 1h; ssl_session_ticket_key rotation should be automated.

title: SSL/TLS Cipher: No Cipher Order Configured
aliases: SSL/TLS Cipher: No Cipher Order Configured
remediation_brief: Enable server-side cipher suite ordering. On Apache: SSLHonorCipherOrder On. On nginx: ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on. Define a strong cipher list that places AEAD ciphers (ECDHE+AESGCM, ECDHE+CHACHA20) first and excludes weak ciphers entirely.
description: The TLS server does not enforce server-side cipher suite ordering, instead accepting the client's preferred cipher suite. Without server-side cipher preference (SSLHonorCipherOrder), a client can negotiate a weak or deprecated cipher suite even if stronger ciphers are available. This allows a downgrade by a malicious client or a MITM that manipulates ClientHello cipher preferences. Server-side ordering ensures the strongest mutually supported cipher is always selected.
impact: Without server-enforced cipher order, the client's cipher preference is used, which may select weaker ciphers over stronger alternatives. An attacker can manipulate the client to negotiate weak ciphers through downgrade attacks.
_x_remediation: Enable server-side cipher suite ordering. On Apache: SSLHonorCipherOrder On. On nginx: ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on. Define a strong cipher list that places AEAD ciphers (ECDHE+AESGCM, ECDHE+CHACHA20) first and excludes weak ciphers entirely.

title: SSL/TLS Ciphers: Obsolete Ciphers
aliases: SSL/TLS Cipher: No Cipher Order Configured
remediation_brief: Audit and update the server's cipher suite configuration. Remove all NULL, EXPORT, RC4, MD5, anon, IDEA, and SEED ciphers. Use a tested cipher string such as the Mozilla TLS configuration generator (ssl-config.mozilla.org) set to 'Intermediate' or 'Modern'. Verify the final cipher list with: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443.
description: The TLS server supports one or more obsolete cipher suites that have been removed from TLS 1.3 and marked as prohibited or deprecated by RFC 8996 and NIST SP 800-52r2. Obsolete cipher suites include those using NULL encryption, EXPORT key exchange, RC4, MD5 MACs, anonymous DH (aNULL/eNULL), or IDEA. Support for these ciphers indicates the server has not been hardened against known cryptographic attacks and may be negotiating weak encryption with vulnerable or misconfigured clients.
impact: Obsolete cipher suites such as RC4 and CBC-mode ciphers are vulnerable to known cryptographic attacks including CVE-2013-2566 (RC4 key stream bias) and CVE-2015-2808 (Bar Mitzvah attack). An attacker performing passive traffic capture can recover plaintext from sessions negotiated with these ciphers, compromising the confidentiality of all transmitted data including credentials and session tokens.
_x_remediation: Audit and update the server's cipher suite configuration. Remove all NULL, EXPORT, RC4, MD5, anon, IDEA, and SEED ciphers. Use a tested cipher string such as the Mozilla TLS configuration generator (ssl-config.mozilla.org) set to 'Intermediate' or 'Modern'. Verify the final cipher list with: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443.

title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160)
remediation_brief: Upgrade OpenSSL to version 1.0.1g or later (or 1.0.2 branch). Revoke and replace the server's TLS certificate and private key immediately — the private key must be assumed compromised. Invalidate all active user sessions. Reissue any client certificates if a client PKI is in use.
description: The target server is confirmed vulnerable to Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160). The OpenSSL heartbeat extension does not properly validate the length field in TLS heartbeat requests, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to read up to 64 KB of server process memory per request. Repeated exploitation can expose TLS private keys, session tokens, plaintext credentials, and other sensitive in-memory data without leaving log entries. This vulnerability is distinct from SS3-010 (which covers testssl detection) — this entry is raised when the Scattershot3 Heartbleed probe module independently confirms the vulnerability.
impact: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160) is a critical memory disclosure vulnerability in OpenSSL that allows an attacker to read up to 64KB of server memory per request without authentication or logging. Leaked memory routinely contains private keys, session tokens, and user credentials, enabling complete compromise of the affected server.
_x_remediation: Upgrade OpenSSL to version 1.0.1g or later (or 1.0.2 branch). Revoke and replace the server's TLS certificate and private key immediately — the private key must be assumed compromised. Invalidate all active user sessions. Reissue any client certificates if a client PKI is in use.

title: EOL Software: OS End-of-Life
remediation_brief: Upgrade the operating system to a supported version immediately. If upgrade is not immediately feasible, isolate the host from untrusted networks, implement compensating controls (host-based IPS, network segmentation, application allowlisting), and create an urgent remediation plan with a defined timeline.
description: The operating system running on this host has reached End-of-Life (EOL) status and is no longer receiving security updates or patches from the vendor. EOL operating systems accumulate unpatched critical vulnerabilities indefinitely and are frequently targeted by automated exploit tools and ransomware families. Any new vulnerability disclosed after the EOL date will remain permanently unpatched on this host, representing an ever-growing attack surface.
impact: An attacker could exploit this to gain full system compromise, execute arbitrary code, or obtain complete unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems. Unpatched software contains known vulnerabilities with potentially available exploit code.
_x_remediation: Upgrade the operating system to a supported version immediately. If upgrade is not immediately feasible, isolate the host from untrusted networks, implement compensating controls (host-based IPS, network segmentation, application allowlisting), and create an urgent remediation plan with a defined timeline.

title: EOL Software: OS End-of-Life (Extended Support)

description: The operating system is within its Extended Support (or Extended Security Updates) period, meaning the vendor continues to provide security patches but only under a paid extended support programme or with limited scope. Standard feature updates and non-security bug fixes may no longer be available. Extended support is a transitional state — the OS will reach full EOL at the extended support end date, and migrations to supported platforms should be planned urgently.
impact: An attacker could leverage this to gain significant unauthorized access, escalate privileges, or exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems. Unpatched software contains known vulnerabilities with potentially available exploit code.
